{"kind":"reasoning","id":"p6-3a4740d7","text":"I now have a good picture of the codebase. Let me summarize what exists:

**Registrations admin page** (`/admin/registrations`):
- Table of AGC registrations (reference, hub, region, delegates, total, mode, status, created)
- Facet filters: region, paymentMode, paymentStatus
- Detail dialog with offline payment info, receipt link, admin message
- Review actions: approve / request correction / reject with optional message (only when `pending_verification`)
- Bulk delete, CSV export (client-side), Excel export (server action)
- Backend: `listAgcRegistrationsAdmin` — collect ALL registrations, N+1 storage.getUrl per record, returns everything reversed. No server-side pagination.

**Accommodation admin page** (`/admin/accommodation`):
- Two tabs: Bookings and Pools
- Bookings tab: stat tiles (total, awaiting review, reserved, confirmed), table with region/booking/payment facets, detail dialog with guests list, offline payment, review actions, bulk delete, per-booking guest CSV
- Pools tab: stat tiles, pool cards with progress bars, reallocation form (type, from scope, to scope, quantity)
- Backend: `listAgcBookingsAdmin` — collect all bookings + guests per booking (N+1), full export of all data to the client.

**Overview** (`/admin`): KPI cards, needs attention, recent activity, charts, housing capacity.

Now let me think about what improvements would be valuable, grounded in what I've seen:

**Performance / architecture:**
1. `listAgcRegistrationsAdmin` and `listAgcBookingsAdmin` load the entire table into the client, with N+1 storage URL resolution per row. As AGC 2026 scales (hundreds/thousands of bookings), this will degrade. Options: server-side pagination with search params, or at least batch receipt URL resolution, or lazy-load receipt URL only when detail dialog opens.
2. `storage.getUrl` per row — receipts are only needed in the detail dialog. Could return a boolean `hasReceipt` and fetch URL on demand via a small query.

**UX improvements — Registrations:**
1. Review actions only appear for `pending_verification` in the detail dialog footer. Inline quick actions in the table row (approve/reject) would speed up bulk review; also bulk approve.
2. Keyboard navigation between pending items (next/prev), a "review queue" mode.
3. Awaiting-review count / stat tiles at top (Bookings tab has them; Registrations tab has none — inconsistency! Registrations page lacks StatTiles).
4. Amount verification: offline.amountPaid vs totalAmount mismatch highlighting (underpayment/overpayment detection).
5. Receipt image preview inline in dialog (if it's an image) rather than just link.
6. Duplicate/late-payment detection (same hub with multiple pending_verification).
7. Admin message history — only `adminMessage` (last message) is shown; there's no conversation thread. Could show audit log entries for that registration (there's an audit page already).
8. Sort defaults, saved views/filters persisted to URL (shareable links).
9. Bulk review actions (approve selected / reject selected) — currently only bulk delete.

**UX improvements — Accommodation:**
1. Guest-level table view (currently one row per booking, guests hidden in dialog). A "Guests" tab: one row per guest, filterable by gender/accommodation type/bishop rate — useful for rooming lists and check-in.
2. Room assignment feature — currently guests are booked into type-level pools, but there's no room-level assignment (no room entity). Privacy policy mentions roommates/rooms. A rooming/assignment module: create rooms per type with capacity, assign guests (single-gender enforcement since gender is captured), print rooming lists.
3. Check-in/check-out status per guest at the event.
4. Pool reallocation form improvements: live preview of from/to pools after reallocation, validation against available, "note" field exists server-side but UI doesn't send it; confirmation dialog; audit trail of reallocations shown.
5. Expiring holds: bookings with `expiresAt` — a visible "holds expiring soon" alert list with the countdown, and ability to nudge the rep (email) or extend the hold.
6. Accommodation occupancy by type × region matrix (who's waiting because their regional pool is empty while global has space) — waitlist visibility.
7. Guest list export is per booking; add "export all guests (filtered)" already exists via exportRows. Fine.

**Cross-cutting:**
1. URL state for filters/search/page so refresh preserves context and links can be shared.
2. Column presets & persistence (localStorage) — currently column visibility resets.
3. Audit trail per record (who approved what, when) surfaced in detail dialog.
4. Email preview: the review flow queues an email; admins can't see what was sent. Show email log link in detail.
5. Accessibility: table row click opens dialog — ensure keyboard operability (row as button). DataTable rows use onClick on TableRow (not focusable). Add keyboard support.
6. Saved views / quick filters like "Awaiting review" as one-click tabs above the table (pending_verification + correction_requested).
7. Real-time updates — Convex queries are reactive already, good. But pagination state may jump when data changes; fine.
8. Mobile: tables scroll horizontally; ok.
9. Print-friendly rooming lists / manifests.
10. Notifications: "needs attention" already exists on overview. Could add badge counts in nav (pending review count next to nav items).

Also potential data-quality: `expiresAt` holds — show which reserved bookings are about to expire (auto-expiry job?). There's presumably a cron. Let me check quickly... Not critical; I can mention.

Also the Registrations page header has export button; the accommodation page doesn't have the Excel export? Let me check — `AgcExcelExportButton` exists with `which: "bookings"`. In AgcAccommodationPage there's no header; the page.tsx for accommodation just renders AgcAccommodationPage. Actually AdminPageHeader with export for bookings seems to exist in hotels page or accommodation page? From earlier read: accommodation/page.tsx has AdminPageHeader description but actions not shown — it only shows description + `<AgcAccommodationPage />`. Let me verify whether AgcExcelExportButton is used with bookings somewhere. Quick search would confirm. Not crucial — I can suggest adding it.

## Review workflow (biggest time-saver during peak)

4. **Bulk review, not just bulk delete.** Both tables only offer bulk *delete*. During AGC surge, hundreds of `pending_verification` receipts will be approved one dialog at a time. Add multi-select → bulk approve (with confirmation) and bulk "request correction" with a shared message.
5. **Receipt-first review mode.** Today the receipt is a link *inside* the dialog. For verification work a side-by-side layout — receipt image left, payment details + amount check right, Approve/Correct/Reject buttons and keyboard shortcuts (`A`/`C`/`R`), auto-advance to next pending row — would cut review time dramatically.
6. **Underpayment flagging.** `offline.amountPaid` vs `totalAmount` is displayed but never compared. Auto-flag mismatches (badge + filter "short paid") — that's the #1 manual check finance does.
7. **Per-record review history.** Rows show only the last `adminMessage`. Audit logs already capture every decision (`agc_registration.approve`, etc.) — surface a small timeline in the detail dialog: who decided, when, what message.
8. **Aging indicators on the queue.** Default tile "Awaiting review" has no sense of urgency — show "oldest waiting 3 days" or badge rows older than 48h, oldest-first sort in the pending filter.

## Accommodation-specific

9. **Room assignment.** There's no rooming concept at all — only type-level pools. Even a light version (assign guests to rooms per type, gender-matched for shared rooms, printable rooming list per hotel) turns the page from "review payments" into an ops tool for check-in week.
10. **Expired-hold visibility.** `expiresAt` exists and a cron reaps lapsed holds, but admins can't see holds about to expire in the next 24/48h or manually release/confirm a lapsed-but-not-yet-reaped booking. A "expiring soon" strip on the Pools tab would answer "what's freeing up?".
11. **Guest context.** Admin sees name/gender/type only — no contact, arrival info, or special requests. If reps collect any of this, surface it in the guest list; if not, add the fields.
12. **Reallocation safety.** The [reallocate form](src/components/admin/agc/PoolsTab.tsx#L153) doesn't validate quantity against the source pool's available count client-side and shows no summary before applying. Add validation + a confirm line ("Move 10 dormitory beds: Africa → Rest of world") and a short history of past reallocations (they're already audited server-side).

## Robustness & polish

13. **Soft delete / trash.** Bulk delete is permanent, releases held inventory, and can't be undone. A 30-day soft-delete with a restore view would de-risk the most destructive action in the UI.
14. **Persist table state in the URL.** Filters, search, and page reset on every navigation; encoding them in query params makes filtered views shareable between admins ("look at these rejected bookings").
15. **Query efficiency.** `listAgcBookingsAdmin` does N+1 queries (guests + storage URL per booking) and both list queries `.collect()` everything. Fine at hundreds of rows; worth server-side pagination before the event spike.
16. **Column picker labels.** The Columns dropdown shows raw ids like `total`/`paymentMode` — capitalize or add display names.

async function purgeRegistrationRecord(
  ctx: MutationCtx,
  record: Doc<"agcRegistrations">,
) {
  if (record.offline?.receiptStorageId) {
    await ctx.storage.delete(record.offline.receiptStorageId);
  }
  await ctx.db.delete(record._id);
}

async function purgeBookingRecord(
  ctx: MutationCtx,
  booking: Doc<"agcBookings">,
) {
  for (const line of await ctx.db
    .query("agcBookingLines")
    .withIndex("by_booking", (q) => q.eq("bookingId", booking._id))
    .collect()) {
    await ctx.db.delete(line._id);
  }
  for (const guest of await ctx.db
    .query("agcGuests")
    .withIndex("by_booking", (q) => q.eq("bookingId", booking._id))
    .collect()) {
    // Drop any room assignment first so room occupancy stays consistent.
    for (const assignment of await ctx.db
      .query("agcRoomAssignments")
      .withIndex("by_guest", (q) => q.eq("guestId", guest._id))
      .collect()) {
      await ctx.db.delete(assignment._id);
    }
    await ctx.db.delete(guest._id);
  }
  // Ledger has no booking index; sweep by bookingId.
  for (const entry of await ctx.db.query("agcInventoryLedger").collect()) {
    if (entry.bookingId === booking._id) await ctx.db.delete(entry._id);
  }
  if (booking.offline?.receiptStorageId) {
    await ctx.storage.delete(booking.offline.receiptStorageId);
  }
  await ctx.db.delete(booking._id);

/** Restore everything deleted more than TTL days ago. Returns rows purged. */
export const purgeExpiredTrash = mutation({
  args: { sessionToken: sessionTokenValidator },
  handler: async (ctx, args) => {
    const actor = await assertTrashPurgeAccess(ctx, args.sessionToken);
    const now = Date.now();
    let purged = 0;
    for (const record of await ctx.db
      .query("agcRegistrations")
      .withIndex("by_deleted_at")
      .collect()) {
      if (!record.deletedAt) continue;
      if (now - record.deletedAt < AGC_TRASH_TTL_MS) continue;
      await purgeRegistrationRecord(ctx, record);
      purged += 1;
    }
    for (const booking of await ctx.db
      .query("agcBookings")
      .withIndex("by_deleted_at")
      .collect()) {
      if (!booking.deletedAt) continue;
      if (now - booking.deletedAt < AGC_TRASH_TTL_MS) continue;
      await purgeBookingRecord(ctx, booking);
      purged += 1;
    }
    if (purged > 0) {
      await writeAuditLog(ctx, {
        actorUserId: actor._id,
        actorEmail: actor.email,
        action: "agc_trash.purged",
        entityType: "agcTrash",
        summary: `Purged ${purged} expired record(s) from trash by ${actor.email}`,
        metadata: { count: purged },
      });
    }
    return { purged };
  },
});

          try {
            const parsed: unknown = JSON.parse(log.metadata);
            return typeof parsed === "object" && parsed !== null && "message" in parsed
              ? ((parsed as { message?: unknown }).message ?? null)
              : null;
          } catch {

/**
 * Reserved holds that lapse within 48 hours — surfaced above the pools
 * grid so admins can see what's about to free up without digging.
 */
export const listExpiringHoldsAdmin = query({
  args: { sessionToken: sessionTokenValidator },
  handler: async (ctx, args) => {
    await requireRole(ctx, args.sessionToken, ["admin", "accommodation", "finance"]);
    const now = Date.now();
    const cutoff = now + 48 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
    const [holds, hubs] = await Promise.all([
      ctx.db
        .query("agcBookings")
        .withIndex("by_expires_at", (q) =>
          q.lte("expiresAt", cutoff),
        )
        .collect(),
      ctx.db.query("agcHubs").collect(),
    ]);
    const hubName = new Map(hubs.map((hub) => [hub._id, hub.name]));
    return holds
      .filter(
        (row) =>
          !row.deletedAt && row.bookingStatus === "reserved" && (row.expiresAt ?? 0) >= now,
      )
      .sort((a, b) => (a.expiresAt ?? 0) - (b.expiresAt ?? 0))
      .slice(0, 10)
      .map((row) => ({
        _id: row._id,
        referenceNumber: row.referenceNumber ?? "",
        hubName: hubName.get(row.hubId) ?? "(unknown)",
        totalAmount: row.totalAmount,
        currency: row.currency,
        expiresAt: row.expiresAt ?? now,
      }));
  },
});

/** Trigger a browser download from a Convex action's base64 payload. */
export function downloadBase64(
  filename: string,
  contentBase64: string,
): void {
  const binary = atob(contentBase64);
  const bytes = new Uint8Array(binary.length);
  for (let i = 0; i < binary.length; i += 1) {
    bytes[i] = binary.charCodeAt(i);
  }
  const blob = new Blob([bytes], {
    type: "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet",
  });
  const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
  const anchor = document.createElement("a");
  anchor.href = url;
  anchor.download = filename;
  anchor.click();
  URL.revokeObjectURL(url);
}

/** Shared export-button wiring for the Registrations and Accommodation pages. */
export function AgcExcelExportButton({
  which,
  label,
}: {
  which: AgcExportKind;
  label: string;
}) {
  const { sessionToken } = useAdminSession();
  const exportBookingsAction = useAction(api.agcExcel.exportBookingsExcel);
  const exportRegistrationsAction = useAction(
    api.agcExcel.exportRegistrationsExcel,
  );
  const [exporting, setExporting] = useState(false);

  const runExport = async () => {
    if (!sessionToken) return;
    setExporting(true);
    try {
      const result =
        which === "bookings"
          ? await exportBookingsAction({ sessionToken })
          : await exportRegistrationsAction({ sessionToken });
      downloadBase64(result.filename, result.contentBase64);
    } catch (err) {
      toast.error(...toastFriendlyErrorParts(err, "Export failed"));
    } finally {
      setExporting(false);
    }
  };

  return (
    <Button
      type="button"
      variant="outline"
      size="sm"
      disabled={exporting}
      onClick={() => void runExport()}
    >
      {exporting ? (
        <Loader2Icon className="size-4 animate-spin" />
      ) : (
        <DownloadIcon className="size-4" />
      )}
      {label}
    </Button>
  );
}

  className,
}: {
  createdAt: number;
  className?: string;
}) {

      )}
    >
      <Clock className="size-3" />
      {days}d
    </Badge>

## What was built

**Backend ([convex/agcAdminData.ts](convex/agcAdminData.ts), [convex/schema.ts](convex/schema.ts), new [convex/agcRoomAssignments.ts](convex/agcRoomAssignments.ts), [convex/crons.ts](convex/crons.ts))**
- **Bulk review**: `bulkReviewAgcRegistrations` / `bulkReviewAgcBookings` — approve or request-correction across up to 200 rows at once, skipping rows not awaiting verification, writing one audit entry, and sending **one summary email per hub** (never per row).
- **Soft delete**: deletes now move rows to a 30-day trash (new `deletedAt` fields + `by_deleted_at` indexes). New `listAgcTrash`, `restoreAgcRegistration/Booking`, `purgeExpiredTrash` (admin) + hourly cron purge. Trashing a reserved booking releases its held rooms immediately; restoring returns it as expired.
- **Room assignment**: new `agcRooms` / `agcRoomAssignments` tables with room CRUD (gender locks, capacity guards), unassigned-guest discovery (confirmed bookings only), assign/move/unassign with type + capacity + gender validation, and a one-click auto-assigner that keeps hub groups together.
- **New queries**: `listAgcRecordHistory` (per-record review timeline from the audit log), `listExpiringHoldsAdmin` (holds lapsing within 48h), `listReallocationsAdmin` (recent pool moves).
- **Dead links fixed**: all `/admin/agc` hrefs in attention cards and quick-search now point to `/admin/registrations` and `/admin/accommodation`.
- List/overview queries filter soft-deleted rows; new schema tables documented in the schema file.

**Frontend**
- [ReviewTools.tsx](src/components/admin/agc/ReviewTools.tsx) (new): **bulk review dialog** with confirmation + shared message, **receipt review queue** — side-by-side receipt vs. payment details, amount-mismatch flag, keyboard shortcuts (`A` approve, `C` correct, `R` reject, `J` skip), auto-advance until the queue is clear — plus the **trash dialog** with restore/purge.
- [AgcAdminClient.tsx](src/components/admin/agc/AgcAdminClient.tsx) (registrations) & [BookingsTab.tsx](src/components/admin/agc/BookingsTab.tsx): stat tiles (registrations now on par with bookings), "Paid ≠ total" [badges](src/components/admin/agc/Badges.tsx), aging badges (amber 1d+, red 3d+), oldest-waiting hint on tiles, bulk review button in the selection bar, per-record **history timeline** in detail dialogs, trash launcher.
- [RoomsTab.tsx](src/components/admin/agc/RoomsTab.tsx) (new, third section on the accommodation page): room grid with live occupancy, add/edit/delete rooms, per-room guest assignment, auto-assign, and a **printable rooming list** with per-type filter, hub + booking ref per guest, and vacant-bed placeholders.
- [PoolsTab.tsx](src/components/admin/agc/PoolsTab.tsx): expiring-holds strip, source-pool availability hint with client-side validation, and a confirmation dialog before every reallocation, with recent reallocation history below.
- [data-table.tsx](src/components/ui/data-table.tsx): optional URL persistence of search/filters/page (`?t=…`, shareable filtered views) and human-readable column labels in the Columns dropdown.
- `?id=` deep links wired into both tabs — command-palette and attention-card links now open the right record's detail dialog.

Two behavior notes: restored bookings come back as *expired* (their hold was released when trashed), and room assignment only admits guests with **confirmed** bookings — matching the payment-first workflow. The new tables will be pushed to your Convex deployment on the next `npx convex dev`/`npx convex deploy`.

  const status = isSmtpConfigured() ? ("pending" as const) : ("stub" as const);
  const emailLogId: Id<"emailLogs"> = await ctx.db.insert("emailLogs", {
    to: rep.email,
    subject: args.subject,
    body: args.body,
    type: args.type,
    referenceId: args.referenceId,
    status,
    createdAt: Date.now(),
  });
  if (status === "pending") {
    await ctx.scheduler.runAfter(0, internal.emailSendAction.sendEmail, {

}

/**
 * A released payment-on-arrival hold is a dead end for the hub unless they are
 * told about it: email the rep and leave the same explanation in the portal,
 * where the booking's adminMessage renders as the desk-notice banner. Both
 * spell out that the beds went back into the pool and how to book again.
 */
async function notifyPoaHoldReleased(
  ctx: MutationCtx,
  booking: Doc<"agcBookings">,
  deadline: number,
  holdHours: number,
) {
  const lines = await ctx.db
    .query("agcBookingLines")
    .withIndex("by_booking", (q) => q.eq("bookingId", booking._id))
    .collect();
  const beds =
    lines
      .sort((a, b) => a.accommodationType.localeCompare(b.accommodationType))
      .map(
        (line) =>
          `${line.quantity} × ${AGC_ACCOMMODATION_TYPES[line.accommodationType]?.label ?? line.accommodationType}`,
      )
      .join(", ") || "The beds";
  const reference = booking.referenceNumber ?? "";
  const releasedOn = new Date(deadline).toUTCString();
  const label = reference ? ` ${reference}` : "";

  // Portal notice on the booking itself (shown as the desk-message banner).
  await ctx.db.patch(booking._id, {
    adminMessage: `Your payment-on-arrival hold${label} expired on ${releasedOn}, so ${beds} went back into the pool. Book again in the Accommodation tab of this portal, or contact the accommodation desk (with this reference) if the booking window has closed.`,
  });

  await queueHoldEmail(ctx, {
    repId: booking.repId,
    subject: `Homecoming 2026 — your beds were released (${reference || "accommodation hold"})`,
    body: [
      `Hello ${reference ? `(${reference})` : ""},`,
      "",
      `Your payment-on-arrival accommodation hold${label} was held for ${holdHours}h and the payment was not confirmed before it expired on ${releasedOn}.`,
      `The beds have gone back into the pool so other hubs can use them: ${beds}.`,
      "",
      "To hold beds again:",
      "  1. Open the representative portal → Accommodation and create a new booking.",
      "  2. Pay by bank transfer/MoMo and upload the receipt in the portal, or pay at the venue desk on arrival, so the desk can confirm the payment and lock the beds in.",
      "",
      "If the booking window has closed, contact the Homecoming 2026 accommodation desk and quote this reference.",
      "",
      "— Homecoming 2026 Accommodation Desk",
    ].join("\n"),
    referenceId: booking._id,
    type: "agc_booking_poa_hold_released",
  });
}

/**
 * Scheduled job: expire bookings whose hold has lapsed (§32–34) — including
 * payment-on-arrival holds, which are on the same 72h window. Expiring returns
 * the held beds to their pools and flips the booking to `expired`.
 *
 * POA reservations created before the hold timer existed carry no `expiresAt`;
 * for those the fallback deadline is their creation time plus the current hold
 * window, so old holds are released too instead of holding beds forever.
 */
export async function expireOverdueHolds(ctx: MutationCtx): Promise<number> {
  const now = Date.now();
  const holdHours = await getHoldHours(ctx);
  const legacyWindow = holdHours * 60 * 60 * 1000;
  const reserved = await ctx.db
    .query("agcBookings")
    .withIndex("by_booking_status", (q) => q.eq("bookingStatus", "reserved"))
    .collect();

  let expired = 0;
  for (const booking of reserved) {
    if (booking.deletedAt) continue;
    const deadline =
      booking.expiresAt ??
      (booking.poa ? booking.createdAt + legacyWindow : undefined);
    if (!deadline || deadline >= now) continue;
    await releaseBookingInventory(ctx, booking, "expire");
    await ctx.db.patch(booking._id, {
      bookingStatus: "expired",
      updatedAt: now,
    });
    // POA holds are the hub's own money promise — tell the rep the beds moved.
    if (booking.poa) {
      await notifyPoaHoldReleased(ctx, booking, deadline, holdHours);
    }
    await writeAuditLog(ctx, {
      actorEmail: "system",
      action: "agc_booking.hold_expired",
      entityType: "agcBookings",
      entityId: booking._id,
      summary: `${booking.poa ? "Payment-on-arrival" : "Unpaid"} hold ${booking.referenceNumber ?? ""} expired — held beds returned to their pools`,
    });
    expired += 1;
  }
  return expired;
}","allowMultiple":false}]}}

## What the rep gets when the 72h window lapses
**[expireOverdueHolds](convex/agcAccommodation.ts#L594)** now calls a new `notifyPoaHoldReleased` for every POA hold it releases, which does two things:

1. **Email** (queued through `emailLogs` like every other portal mail — sent immediately when SMTP is configured, logged as a stub otherwise): subject `Homecoming 2026 — your beds were released (REF)`. The body names the hold window and expiry instant, lists exactly what was released (`2 × Dormitory (Mighty Fortress)`), and gives the re-book path — create a new booking in the portal → Accommodation, pay by bank/MoMo and upload the receipt (or pay at the desk) so the desk can confirm and lock the beds in — closing with the desk contact if the booking window has already shut.
2. **Portal notice**: the same explanation is written to the booking's `adminMessage`, which the representative portal already renders as the desk-message banner on the booking card. Expired bookings stay visible under the "all"/"closed" filters (default is "all"), so the notice is the first thing the hub sees when they open the tab.

Plain offline holds still expire silently — that path is unchanged, since the request was specific to payment-on-arrival terms.

async function notifyPoaHoldReleased(
  ctx: MutationCtx,
  booking: Doc<"agcBookings">,
  deadline: number,
  holdHours: number,

  const lines = await ctx.db
    .query("agcBookingLines")
    .withIndex("by_booking", (q) => q.eq("bookingId", booking._id))
    .collect();
  const beds =
    lines
      .sort((a, b) => a.accommodationType.localeCompare(b.accommodationType))
      .map(
        (line) =>
          `${line.quantity} × ${AGC_ACCOMMODATION_TYPES[line.accommodationType]?.label ?? line.accommodationType}`,
      )
      .join(", ") || "The beds";
  const reference = booking.referenceNumber ?? "";
  const releasedOn = new Date(deadline).toUTCString();
  const label = reference ? ` ${reference}` : "";
  const rep = await ctx.db.get(booking.repId);
  const greeting = rep?.firstName ?? rep?.username ?? "there";

// ------------------------------------------------------------------
// Releases (expiry, cancellation)
// ------------------------------------------------------------------

export async function releaseBookingInventory(
  ctx: MutationCtx,
  booking: Doc<"agcBookings">,
  action: "release" | "expire" | "cancel",
) {
  const lines = await ctx.db
    .query("agcBookingLines")
    .withIndex("by_booking", (q) => q.eq("bookingId", booking._id))
    .collect();

  for (const line of lines) {
    const pool = await getPoolForRegion(
      ctx,
      line.accommodationType,
      booking.region,
    );
    // Confirmed bookings keep their units consumed — only reserved units return.
    if (booking.bookingStatus === "confirmed") continue;
    await releaseUnits(ctx, pool, line.quantity, booking._id, action);
  }
}

/** Scheduled job: expire reserved bookings whose hold has lapsed (§32–34). */
export async function expireOverdueHolds(ctx: MutationCtx): Promise<number> {
  const now = Date.now();
  const reserved = await ctx.db
    .query("agcBookings")
    .withIndex("by_booking_status", (q) => q.eq("bookingStatus", "reserved"))
    .collect();

  let expired = 0;
  for (const booking of reserved) {
    // POA holds are never on a timer — they expire only when the hub cancels.
    if (booking.poa) continue;
    if (!booking.expiresAt || booking.expiresAt >= now) continue;
    await releaseBookingInventory(ctx, booking, "expire");
    await ctx.db.patch(booking._id, {
      bookingStatus: "expired",
      updatedAt: now,
    });
    expired += 1;
  }
  return expired;
}

export type SubstitutionCheck =
  | { ok: true }
  | { ok: false; reason: string };

export function checkSubstitution(
  previous: Pick<
    Doc<"agcGuests">,
    "gender" | "accommodationType" | "status"
  >,
  next: { gender: AgcGender; accommodationType: AgcAccommodationType },
  allowOverride: boolean,
): SubstitutionCheck {
  if (previous.status !== "active") {
    return { ok: false, reason: "This guest is not active" };
  }
  const sameGender = previous.gender === next.gender;
  const sameType = previous.accommodationType === next.accommodationType;
  if (sameGender && sameType) return { ok: true };
  if (allowOverride) return { ok: true };
  return {
    ok: false,
    reason: `Substitutions must keep the same gender and accommodation type (was ${previous.gender} ${previous.accommodationType})`,
  };

Availability/pricing stay live, so a pool that filled up in the meantime blocks the reserve button instead of over-booking. If the roster was emptied, it falls back to one blank row per bed line so the same types come back; if the form already has rows it appends rather than discarding typed work.

## Confirmed records can’t be deleted
`deleteAgcRegistration` / `deleteAgcBooking` now throw for a confirmed record, and the bulk variants skip confirmed rows (an all-confirmed selection is refused, a mixed one deletes the rest and returns `skippedConfirmed`) — [agcAdminData.ts](convex/agcAdminData.ts#L2098). ## Expired bookings back into their pools
[reconcileExpiredBookingInventory](convex/agcAccommodation.ts#L624) expires lapsed holds first, then walks every `expired`/`cancelled` booking and returns the beds it still holds — from `confirmed` for beds that were paid for, from `reserved` otherwise, always into the pool matching the line’s type and the booking’s region. It uses the inventory ledger to subtract what each booking already gave back, so it’s idempotent. Exposed to admins as “Move expired bookings back to pools” in the Pools tab and to you as a CLI one-off: I ran `npx convex run crons:reconcileExpiredBookingsOnce` against the dev deployment and it came back `{"expiredHolds":0,"bookings":0,"units":0}` — nothing was leaking there, the 5-minute cron already keeps it clean.

[listAgcBookingsAdmin](convex/agcAdminData.ts#L1870) returns every non-POA, non-deleted booking, so the Accommodation → **Bookings** tab listed `expired` and `cancelled` rows alongside live ones (they were also counted in the "Total bookings" tile). Only POA rows were kept out of that table.

[BookingsTab.tsx](src/components/admin/agc/BookingsTab.tsx) starts on **live reservations only** — reserved, awaiting review, correction, confirmed. /**
 * A booking is roomable once it is paid+confirmed — or while it is on
 * payment-on-arrival terms (beds are held, payment credited later).
 */
export function isRoomableBooking(booking: {
  deletedAt?: number;
  bookingStatus: string;
  paymentMode: string;
  poa?: { status: string } | null;
}): boolean {
  if (booking.deletedAt !== undefined) return false;
  if (booking.bookingStatus === "confirmed") return true;
  return (
    booking.paymentMode === "payment_on_arrival" &&
    booking.bookingStatus === "reserved" &&
    booking.poa?.status !== "confirmed" // (defensive; confirmed implies bookingStatus confirmed)
  );
}

/**

 * delegate sits in the room, and the count stays stable as guests move out.
 */
function bedNumbersByGuest(
  assignments: Doc<"agcRoomAssignments">[],
): Map<string, number> {
  const byRoom = new Map<string, Doc<"agcRoomAssignments">[]>();
  for (const assignment of assignments) {
    if (assignment.endedAt !== undefined) continue;
    const rows = byRoom.get(assignment.roomId) ?? [];
    rows.push(assignment);
    byRoom.set(assignment.roomId, rows);
  }
  const beds = new Map<string, number>();
  for (const rows of byRoom.values()) {
    rows.sort((a, b) => a.createdAt - b.createdAt);
    rows.forEach((assignment, index) => beds.set(assignment.guestId, index + 1));
  }
  return beds;
}

/**
 * A booking is roomable once it is paid+confirmed — or while it is on
 * payment-on-arrival terms (beds are held, payment credited later).
 */
export function isRoomableBooking(booking: {
  deletedAt?: number;
  bookingStatus: string;
  paymentMode: string;
  poa?: { status: string } | null;
}): boolean {
  if (booking.deletedAt !== undefined) return false;
  if (booking.bookingStatus === "confirmed") return true;
  return (
    booking.paymentMode === "payment_on_arrival" &&
    booking.bookingStatus === "reserved" &&
    booking.poa?.status !== "confirmed" // (defensive; confirmed implies bookingStatus confirmed)
  );
}

/**
 * Bed number per guest: the guest's position among the room's open

 * delegate sits in the room, and the count stays stable as guests move out.
 */
function bedNumbersByGuest(
  assignments: Doc<"agcRoomAssignments">[],
): Map<string, number> {
  const byRoom = new Map<string, Doc<"agcRoomAssignments">[]>();
  for (const assignment of assignments) {
    if (assignment.endedAt !== undefined) continue;
    const rows = byRoom.get(assignment.roomId) ?? [];
    rows.push(assignment);
    byRoom.set(assignment.roomId, rows);
  }
  const beds = new Map<string, number>();
  for (const rows of byRoom.values()) {
    rows.sort((a, b) => a.createdAt - b.createdAt);
    rows.forEach((assignment, index) => beds.set(assignment.guestId, index + 1));
  }
  return beds;
}

/**
 * A booking is roomable once it is paid+confirmed — or while it is on
 * payment-on-arrival terms (beds are held, payment credited later).
 */
export function isRoomableBooking(booking: {
  deletedAt?: number;
  bookingStatus: string;
  paymentMode: string;
  poa?: { status: string } | null;
}): boolean {
  if (booking.deletedAt !== undefined) return false;
  if (booking.bookingStatus === "confirmed") return true;
  return (
    booking.paymentMode === "payment_on_arrival" &&
    booking.bookingStatus === "reserved" &&
    booking.poa?.status !== "confirmed" // (defensive; confirmed implies bookingStatus confirmed)
  );
}

I've implemented the mock's two screens where those workflows actually live in this app.

**Assignments screen → arrival desk** ([ArrivalPage.tsx](src/components/admin/agc/ArrivalPage.tsx#L496)). The desk now opens with the mock's layout: a large "Search name, hub, room number or booking ref" field with a **Search** button, gender pills plus hub / room-type / location filters and **Clear filters**, a roster table with **Room · Bed · Name · Gender · Hub · Check-in · Key**, and a sticky detail card for the selected delegate ([line 721](src/components/admin/agc/ArrivalPage.tsx#L721)). The card shows paid room type, location including bed, status, payment and key, with **Check in**, **Check out**, **Correct check-in**, **Mark key returned** and **Move delegate** as the roles allow. Clicking a name or row selects it; the existing check-in, override, key-recipient and move dialogs are unchanged. The dense stats / group check-in / offline station / keys / sync panels are preserved under a collapsible **Desk overview & tools** strip ([line 874](src/components/admin/agc/ArrivalPage.tsx#L874)), and `DeskAlerts` stays at the top.

To feed the new columns I extended the desk queries ([agcCheckin.ts](convex/agcCheckin.ts#L82)): **bed** is the delegate's position among the room's open assignments, and **key** maps the room's key record to Issued / Returned / Pending / — (wristband rooms show —). Search also now matches room, building and booking reference. The mock's plain "Not yet" would hide why a delegate can't be checked in, so blocked rows read **No room** or **Payment first** in amber ([line 1126](src/components/admin/agc/ArrivalPage.tsx#L1126)).

**Bulk assign screen → Rooms tab** ([BulkAssignPanel.tsx](src/components/admin/agc/BulkAssignPanel.tsx#L51)). The old compact unassigned list is replaced by the mock's two-pane view: tick delegates on the left (gender pills, hub/type/name filters, **Select all shown**, **Clear**), pick a room on the right from cards showing type, free beds and gender lock, then **Assign N to Room X**. Guests that don't fit the chosen room are disabled and dropped from the selection, select-all caps at the free beds, and the button explains over-capacity rather than letting the server reject the batch. It's wired to the existing `assignGuests` mutation, so capacity and single-gender rules still enforce server-side. The desk has a **Bulk assign** shortcut for admin/accommodation roles ([line 623](src/components/admin/agc/ArrivalPage.tsx#L623)), and `/admin/accommodation?tab=rooms` now deep-links to that tab ([page.tsx](src/app/admin/(console)/accommodation/page.tsx#L29)).

**Choices and gaps:** I kept the app's gold/ink design tokens rather than copying the mock's teal palette, and used the app's existing badge/table/button primitives so it sits inside the console chrome. The mock's separate **Issue key** button has no backend equivalent — key issuance remains part of check-in (the card says so) — and **Flag this record for review** has no store to write to, so I left it out rather than create a dead-end flag table. Both would be small follow-ups if you want them.

**Verified:** `npx tsc --noEmit` ✓, `npm run lint` ✓ 0 problems, `npx vitest run` 198/198 ✓, `npm run build` ✓ — all on the final files. A fresh dev server is running on `:3000` and both routes return 200; the served arrival chunk contains the new roster and `Payment first` logic, and the accommodation chunk contains the bulk panel. The Preview panel is registered at `http://127.0.0.1:3000/admin/arrival`; I could not verify the signed-in rendering myself because the console requires staff credentials and the preview starts at the sign-in door. The dev server's HMR WebSocket handshake fails in this environment (visible in console before and after my changes) but page loads and compiled chunks are healthy. Changes are uncommitted.

Signing in there is the quickest way to confirm the card actions and the bulk panel against real data.

  role: "admin" | "accommodation" | "room_assignment" | "checkin" | "finance" | "registration",
) {
  const { createHash, randomBytes } = await import("node:crypto");
  const token = createHash("sha256")
    .update(randomBytes(24))
    .digest("hex");
  const userId = await t.run(async (ctx) => {
    const id = await ctx.db.insert("users", {
      name: `${role}`,
      email: `${role}@example.com`,
      passwordHash: "not-a-real-hash",
      role,
      active: true,
      createdAt: Date.now(),
    });
    await ctx.db.insert("sessions", {
      userId: id,
      token,
      expiresAt: Date.now() + 3_600_000,
      createdAt: Date.now(),
    });
    return id;
  });
  return { token, userId };
}

/**
 * Raise a review flag on a delegate's arrival record. Any desk role may raise
 * one; the note is mandatory because a flag without a reason gives the
 * Accommodation Admin nothing to act on. The record stays on the desk — a flag
 * never blocks a check-in, it just asks for a second look.
 */
export const flagCheckInRecord = mutation({
  args: {
    sessionToken: v.string(),
    guestId: v.id("agcGuests"),
    note: v.string(),
  },
  handler: async (ctx, args) => {
    const actor = await requireRole(ctx, args.sessionToken, [...CHECKIN_ROLES]);
    const note = args.note.trim();
    if (!note) throw new ConvexError("A note is required to flag a record for review");

    const guest = await ctx.db.get(args.guestId);
    if (!guest || guest.status !== "active") {
      throw new ConvexError("Delegate not found or no longer active");
    }
    const existing = await openReviewFlag(ctx, guest._id);
    if (existing) {
      throw new ConvexError(
        `ALREADY FLAGGED — ${existing.note} (raised by ${existing.raisedBy})`,
      );
    }

    // Snapshot where the record sat when it was flagged, so the review still
    // reads correctly after a room move.
    const assignment = await ctx.db
      .query("agcRoomAssignments")
      .withIndex("by_guest", (q) => q.eq("guestId", guest._id))
      .unique();
    const room =
      assignment && assignment.endedAt === undefined
        ? await ctx.db.get(assignment.roomId)
        : null;
    const checkIn = await activeCheckIn(ctx, guest._id);

    const flagId = await ctx.db.insert("agcCheckinFlags", {
      guestId: guest._id,
      bookingId: guest.bookingId,
      roomId: room?._id,
      roomName: room?.name,
      checkInId: checkIn?._id,
      note,
      raisedAt: Date.now(),
      raisedBy: actor.email,
      raisedByRole: actor.role,
    });

    await writeAuditLog(ctx, {
      actorUserId: actor._id,
      actorEmail: actor.email,
      action: "agc_checkin.review_flagged",
      entityType: "agcCheckinFlags",
      entityId: flagId,
      summary: `Flagged ${guestLabel(guest)} for review by ${actor.email} — ${note}`,
      metadata: {
        guestId: guest._id,
        roomId: room?._id,
        checkInId: checkIn?._id,
        note,
      },
    });

    return { flagId };
  },
});

/**
 * Clear a review flag with the outcome of the review — Accommodation Admin
 * only. The flag row is kept with both notes, so what the desk raised and what
 * the reviewer decided stay in the record.
 */
export const resolveCheckinFlag = mutation({
  args: {
    sessionToken: v.string(),
    flagId: v.id("agcCheckinFlags"),
    resolutionNote: v.string(),
  },
  handler: async (ctx, args) => {
    const actor = await requireRole(ctx, args.sessionToken, [...APPROVER_ROLES]);
    const note = args.resolutionNote.trim();
    if (!note) throw new ConvexError("A note is required to clear a review flag");

    const flag = await ctx.db.get(args.flagId);
    if (!flag) throw new ConvexError("Review flag not found");
    if (flag.resolvedAt !== undefined) {
      throw new ConvexError("This review flag is already closed");
    }

    await ctx.db.patch(flag._id, {
      resolvedAt: Date.now(),
      resolvedBy: actor.email,
      resolutionNote: note,
    });

    const guest = await ctx.db.get(flag.guestId);
    await writeAuditLog(ctx, {
      actorUserId: actor._id,
      actorEmail: actor.email,
      action: "agc_checkin.review_cleared",
      entityType: "agcCheckinFlags",
      entityId: flag._id,
      summary: `Cleared the review flag on ${guest ? guestLabel(guest) : "delegate"} by ${actor.email} — ${note}`,
      metadata: { guestId: flag.guestId, raisedBy: flag.raisedBy, note },
    });

    return { success: true as const };
  },
});

Done — the flag action is on the desk, and everything is committed and pushed.

**What staff get.** On the arrival desk, the selected delegate's card now has a **Flag for review** action ([ArrivalPage.tsx](src/components/admin/agc/ArrivalPage.tsx#L898)) for every check-in role. It opens a dialog whose note is **required** — the button stays disabled until something is typed — and the note is what the reviewer reads. Raising a flag writes an audit entry and shows up three ways: a **Review** marker beside the name on the roster, *n* **flagged for review** on the desk alert strip, and an amber banner in the card carrying the note, who raised it and when. A flag never blocks a check-in; it only asks for a second look. Whoever holds `admin`/`accommodation` also gets **Clear flag** in that banner, which needs the review outcome as its own note — only approvers can clear one, and the closed flag keeps both the reason and the outcome in the record.

**Backend.** A new `agcCheckinFlags` table stores the reason, raiser, role, and the room/check-in snapshot at the time, plus the resolution ([schema.ts](convex/schema.ts#L668)). `flagCheckInRecord` refuses an empty note and refuses a second flag while one is open; `resolveCheckinFlag` is approver-only, requires its own note, and refuses to close twice ([agcCheckin.ts](convex/agcCheckin.ts#L696)). Both the desk sheet and delegate search now carry the open flag, and the overview reports the open count.

**Verified.** `npx tsc --noEmit` ✓, `npm run lint` ✓ 0 problems, `npx vitest run` **234/234** ✓, `npm run build` ✓. The new test in [agcPhase2.test.ts](tests/agcPhase2.test.ts#L1122) drives the whole flow: blank note refused, flag visible on the desk sheet and search, duplicate flag refused, check-in still succeeds while flagged, overview counts it, desk role refused on clearing, blank clearing note refused, cleared record unflagged with both notes retained, and a second close refused.

**Commit and push.** `git push` was initially rejected — another thread had pushed 12 commits. I rebased onto them (clean, and the only overlapping hunk was a search guard in the desk query, which merged without conflict), re-ran typecheck, lint, the full suite and the build on the combined tree, then pushed. Everything is in **23958a1** on `origin/master`, including the previously uncommitted roster sheet and bulk-assign panel you asked me to commit. The working tree is clean.

One limitation: I did not visually confirm the dialogs in a browser, since `/admin/arrival` needs staff credentials and you already have a dev server running in your terminal — the flag path is covered by the test rather than by eye.

The obvious next step is giving the Accommodation Admin a single queue to work through, since right now flags are visible per-record on the desk sheet.

```ts
/**
 * Pre-authorize the §18 payment override for a flagged record — Accommodation
 * Admin only. The desk raises the flag when a delegate arrives without a
 * confirmed payment; this is the reviewer's answer, and it is what lets the
 * desk check that delegate in without an approver standing at the counter. The
 * authorization stays on the flag row, so the review keeps its own decision.
 */
export const authorizeCheckinOverride = mutation({
  args: {
    sessionToken: v.string(),
    flagId: v.id("agcCheckinFlags"),
    reason: v.string(),
  },
  handler: async (ctx, args) => {
    const actor = await requireRole(ctx, args.sessionToken, [...APPROVER_ROLES]);
    const reason = args.reason.trim();
    if (!reason) throw new ConvexError("A reason is required to authorize a payment override");

    const flag = await ctx.db.get(args.flagId);
    if (!flag) throw new ConvexError("Review flag not found");
    if (flag.resolvedAt !== undefined) throw new ConvexError("This review flag is already closed");
    if (flag.override) throw new ConvexError(`A payment override is already authorized by ${flag.override.authorizedBy}`);

    const guest = await ctx.db.get(flag.guestId);
    if (!guest || guest.status !== "active") throw new ConvexError("Delegate not found or no longer active");
    const booking = await ctx.db.get(guest.bookingId);
    if (booking && isRoomableBooking(booking)) {
      throw new ConvexError("This booking's payment is in order — no override is needed");
    }

    await ctx.db.patch(flag._id, {
      override: { authorizedBy: actor.email, reason, authorizedAt: Date.now() },
    });

    await writeAuditLog(ctx, {
      actorUserId: actor._id,
      actorEmail: actor.email,
      action: "agc_checkin.override_authorized",
      entityType: "agcCheckinFlags",
      entityId: flag._id,
      summary: `Pre-authorized a payment override for ${guestLabel(guest)} by ${actor.email} — ${reason}`,
      metadata: { guestId: guest._id, bookingId: guest.bookingId, reason, flagId: flag._id },
    });

    return { success: true as const };
  },
});
```

Both requests are done, verified and pushed as **dec1861** on `origin/master` (working tree clean).

**Yes — it can be done, and it now is.** Correcting a delegate was impossible for anyone: [substituteGuest](convex/agcBookings.ts#L647) is the rep's own flow and it refuses once a booking is locked, and the admin-override branch of the substitution helper had never been wired to anything. So a bed handed to another delegate, or a gender recorded in error, had no path to correction anywhere in the console.

**What super admins get.** On Accommodation → Bookings, opening a reservation shows each delegate with a **Correct** action (visible only to the `admin` role — the same role the codebase calls the super admin). The dialog edits title, name and gender, requires a reason, and saves through a new [correctBookingGuest](convex/agcAdminData.ts#L2013). The replaced details go into `agcSubstitutions` with `overrideByAdmin` and the admin's email, the change lands in the audit log, and the accommodation type never moves (§43). Two guards matter: a correction is refused when nothing actually changed, and a **gender change is refused while the delegate sits in a room it would make invalid** — a room locked to the other gender, or a dormitory/hostel room sharing a bed with the old gender. Rooming rules are enforced at allocation, so I check them again rather than quietly rewriting a room's gender composition. To change a gender, the delegate is moved out first; the refusal says so.

**The reviewer can now act from the queue.** The flag dialog on [ReviewFlagsTab.tsx](src/components/admin/agc/ReviewFlagsTab.tsx) gained two decision blocks beside the outcome note. *Room* beds an unroomed delegate from the rooms that fit them — same type, a free bed, no conflicting gender lock — and refuses to guess at shared-room rules, since the server still owns those. *Payment override (§18)* pre-authorizes the override with a required reason, recorded on the flag row ([schema.ts](convex/schema.ts#L680)). That authorization is real, not a note: [performCheckIn](convex/agcCheckin.ts#L437) honours it, so the desk checks the delegate in without an approver at the counter, the arrival stores the authorizer and reason on the check-in, and the audit line reads "pre-authorized by …". The desk's own check-in dialog ([ArrivalPage.tsx](src/components/admin/agc/ArrivalPage.tsx#L1063)) shows the authorization and stops demanding a reason it already has. Authorizing on a booking whose payment is already in order is refused, as is a second authorization, a dead booking, and the desk role attempting it at all.

**Verified.** `npx tsc --noEmit` ✓, `npm run lint` ✓ 0 problems, `npx vitest run` **237/237** ✓, `npm run build` ✓. Two new tests in [agcPhase2.test.ts](tests/agcPhase2.test.ts#L1325): the first drives the queue end to end — unassigned row, the pickable-room filter, assignment, the override refused on a paid booking, reason and role enforcement, duplicate refusal, the desk row carrying the authorization, then the desk checking in on it with the check-in naming the accommodation admin; the second drives the correction — the role gate, blank reason, blank name, no-op, a name-only fix with its history row, the single-gender refusal, the same change succeeding once the bed is vacated, the gender-locked refusal, and both audit entries.

**Limitations worth naming.** I did not click through the dialogs in a browser — the console needs staff credentials and you already have a dev server running, so the flows are covered by the tests rather than by eye. The override deliberately does not confirm the payment or unlock rooming: a booking whose payment is unverified still cannot be bedded (rooming requires confirmed or POA terms), and the queue says so instead of failing at the server. Corrections work on any live booking (confirmed, reserved, pending) rather than confirmed only, since the problem also exists before confirmation; expired and cancelled bookings are refused, matching the substitution rule. And only unroomed delegates can be bedded from the queue — moving someone stays a room change with its own reason on the Rooms tab.

A natural next step is the other half of that gap: the same correction on the arrival desk, where staff actually discover a wrong name or gender mid-check-in, gated to the admin role that the desk already recognises.

test("the desk row carries the delegate's name parts so a super admin can correct them where they are found", async () => {
  const t = createTestConvex();
  const desk = await seedStaff(t, "checkin");
  const admin = await seedStaff(t, "admin");
  const booking = await seedConfirmedBooking(t, {
    accommodationType: "hostel",
    gender: "male",
    count: 1,
  });
  const guestId = booking.guestIds[0] as Id<"agcGuests">;

  // The desk sheet and the search both carry the parts of the name, not just the
  // joined label, so the correction form opens pre-filled with what is on file
  // instead of asking staff to retype a name they are trying to fix.
  const sheet = await t.query(api.agcCheckin.listArrivalDesk, {
    sessionToken: desk.token,
  });
  const sheetRow = sheet.find((row) => row.guestId === guestId);
  expect(sheetRow?.title).toBe("Member");
  expect(sheetRow?.firstName).toBe("Guest0");
  expect(sheetRow?.lastName).toBe("Mensah");
  expect(sheetRow?.name).toContain("Guest0");
  const searched = await t.query(api.agcCheckin.searchDelegates, {
    sessionToken: desk.token,
    search: "Guest0",
  });
  expect(searched[0]).toMatchObject({
    title: "Member",
    firstName: "Guest0",
    lastName: "Mensah",
  });

  // The desk can raise the correction, but making it is still a super admin
  // decision — the counter staff cannot rewrite a record on their own.
  await expect(() =>
    t.mutation(api.agcAdminData.correctBookingGuest, {
      sessionToken: desk.token,
      guestId,
      firstName: "Ama",
      lastName: "Boateng",
      gender: "female",
      reason: "Substituted on arrival",
    }),
  ).rejects.toThrow(/Unauthorized/);

  // Corrected where the desk found it: the counter keeps looking at the same
  // delegate and now sees the name and gender that actually arrived.
  await t.mutation(api.agcAdminData.correctBookingGuest, {
    sessionToken: admin.token,
    guestId,
    firstName: "Ama",
    lastName: "Boateng",
    gender: "female",
    reason: "Substituted on arrival",
  });
  const after = await t.query(api.agcCheckin.listArrivalDesk, {
    sessionToken: desk.token,
  });
  const afterRow = after.find((row) => row.guestId === guestId);
  expect(afterRow?.firstName).toBe("Ama");
  expect(afterRow?.lastName).toBe("Boateng");
  expect(afterRow?.gender).toBe("female");
  expect(afterRow?.name).toContain("Ama");
  expect(afterRow?.name).not.toContain("Guest0");

  // The desk-driven correction is recorded like any other, so the reviewer can
  // see who changed the record and why.
  const audit = await t.run(async (ctx) =>
    (await ctx.db.query("auditLogs").collect()).filter(
      (log) => log.action === "agc_guest.corrected",
    ),
  );
  expect(audit).toHaveLength(1);
  expect(audit[0].actorEmail).toBe("admin@example.com");
  expect(audit[0].summary).toContain("reason: Substituted on arrival");
});

The second is that the card is re-read from the live queries, so once a super admin saves, the counter keeps looking at the same delegate and sees the corrected name and gender immediately — no reload, no stale roster.

I placed the action with the other exceptional desk actions, below check-in/check-out and the garden-variety row moves, and it does not depend on check-in status: a name is wrong whether or not the delegate has arrived, which is precisely when the desk finds out.

**The gate.** The desk can raise the correction, but making it remains a super admin decision — the `checkin` role and the accommodation admin both get `Unauthorized` from the server, so I did not surface a button that would fail. The counter staff see nothing; an accommodation admin sees a one-line note explaining who can make the change, the same honesty the Bookings screen uses. I deliberately did not loosen that boundary, since it was set in the previous change and you asked for the desk to *reach* the correction, not to widen who may make it.

**Verified.** `npx tsc --noEmit` ✓, `npm run lint` ✓ 0 problems, `npx vitest run` **238/238** ✓, `npm run build` ✓. One new test in [agcPhase2.test.ts](tests/agcPhase2.test.ts#L1712) covers the desk path: the sheet and search rows carry the name parts, the desk role is refused, the super admin's correction lands, and the desk's next read shows the new name and gender with the old name gone — plus the audit entry naming the admin and the reason.

**Limitations.** I did not click the dialog in a browser — the console needs staff credentials and you have your own dev server, so the flow is covered by the test rather than by eye. Correction remains super-admin-only, as above. And the same gap still exists in the review queue: a flagged record with a wrong name can be roomed and overridden from the queue, but its name still cannot be corrected there.

+test("the desk row carries the delegate's name parts so a super admin can correct them where they are found", async () => {
+  const t = createTestConvex();
+  const desk = await seedStaff(t, "checkin");
+  const admin = await seedStaff(t, "admin");
+  const booking = await seedConfirmedBooking(t, {
+    accommodationType: "hostel",
+    gender: "male",
+    count: 1,
+  });
+  const guestId = booking.guestIds[0] as Id<"agcGuests">;
+
+  // The desk sheet and the search both carry the parts of the name, not just the
+  // joined label, so the correction form opens pre-filled with what is on file
+  // instead of asking staff to retype a name they are trying to fix.
+  const sheet = await t.query(api.agcCheckin.listArrivalDesk, {
+    sessionToken: desk.token,
+  });
+  const sheetRow = sheet.find((row) => row.guestId === guestId);
+  expect(sheetRow?.title).toBe("Member");
+  expect(sheetRow?.firstName).toBe("Guest0");
+  expect(sheetRow?.lastName).toBe("Mensah");
+  expect(sheetRow?.name).toContain("Guest0");
+  const searched = await t.query(api.agcCheckin.searchDelegates, {
+    sessionToken: desk.token,
+    search: "Guest0",
+  });
+  expect(searched[0]).toMatchObject({
+    title: "Member",
+    firstName: "Guest0",
+    lastName: "Mensah",
+  });
+
+  // The desk can raise the correction, but making it is still a super admin
+  // decision — the counter staff cannot rewrite a record on their own.
+  await expect(() =>
+    t.mutation(api.agcAdminData.correctBookingGuest, {
+      sessionToken: desk.token,
+      guestId,
+      firstName: "Ama",
+      lastName: "Boateng",
+      gender: "female",
+      reason: "Substituted on arrival",
+    }),
+  ).rejects.toThrow(/Unauthorized/);
+
+  // Corrected where the desk found it: the counter keeps looking at the same
+  // delegate and now sees the name and gender that actually arrived.
+  await t.mutation(api.agcAdminData.correctBookingGuest, {
+    sessionToken: admin.token,
+    guestId,
+    firstName: "Ama",
+    lastName: "Boateng",
+    gender: "female",
+    reason: "Substituted on arrival",
+  });
+  const after = await t.query(api.agcCheckin.listArrivalDesk, {
+    sessionToken: desk.token,
+  });
+  const afterRow = after.find((row) => row.guestId === guestId);
+  expect(afterRow?.firstName).toBe("Ama");
+  expect(afterRow?.lastName).toBe("Boateng");
+  expect(afterRow?.gender).toBe("female");
+  expect(afterRow?.name).toContain("Ama");
+  expect(afterRow?.name).not.toContain("Guest0");
+
+  // The desk-driven correction is recorded like any other, so the reviewer can
+  // see who changed the record and why.
+  const audit = await t.run(async (ctx) =>
+    (await ctx.db.query("auditLogs").collect()).filter(
+      (log) => log.action === "agc_guest.corrected",
+    ),
+  );
+  expect(audit).toHaveLength(1);
+  expect(audit[0].actorEmail).toBe("admin@example.com");
+  expect(audit[0].summary).toContain("reason: Substituted on arrival");
+});

Done and pushed as **2b5d263** on `origin/master` (`53b1546..2b5d263`, working tree clean).

**What changed.** The permission is one server check, so I changed it once and then followed it through everywhere the capability appears. [correctBookingGuest](convex/agcAdminData.ts#L2068) now accepts `admin` **or** `accommodation` instead of `requireAdmin`, and the three screens that offer the correction — the review queue, the arrival desk and the bookings list — all now show it to the Accommodation Admin. I deliberately did not limit it to the queue alone: the same mutation is what every entry point calls, so hiding the button on the desk and the bookings list while the role held the power would have been a fake restriction that just pushed admins back to a screen the accommodation team can already reach.

**Who still cannot.** Ordinary desk staff (`checkin`, `room_assignment`). They raise the flag that opens the review in the first place, and the desk tells them the accommodation team corrects the record rather than showing a button that would fail. Removing the gate from the queue let me delete a now-dead branch there: the whole tab is behind the accommodation area guard *and* the server's approver check, so everyone who can open it also holds the power — I left a comment saying so, since that's exactly the kind of assumption a later reader would want to see stated rather than inferred from a missing condition.

**Attribution matters here.** Nothing about who changed what got looser. The substitution history and the audit log name the actual actor, so an Accommodation Admin's correction is recorded as theirs, not as a super admin's — which is the point when the reason for the correction is a substitution that was itself assigned wrongly. I left the existing `overrideByAdmin` history field alone: it marks that the admin-level override was used, and renaming a schema field would need a migration for cosmetic gain.

**Verified.** `npx tsc --noEmit` ✓, `npm run lint` ✓ 0 problems, `npx vitest run` **239/239** ✓, `npm run build` ✓. The two tests that asserted the old gate were rewritten rather than deleted: the correction test now seeds a desk staff and asserts the *desk* is refused, then ends by proving an Accommodation Admin's correction lands with their email in the audit log and the history; the queue test similarly refuses the desk and performs the correction as the Accommodation Admin, asserting the queue re-reads with the new name and gender and the audit line names them.

**Limitations.** Same as before — no browser pass, since the console needs staff credentials and you have a dev server running, so this is covered by tests and type checks rather than by eye. The permission is role-wide rather than scoped to the queue, as explained above; if you'd rather the Accommodation Admin could only correct from the queue and not from the bookings list, say so and I'll scope it per surface.

Worth knowing: nothing yet tells a super admin that an Accommodation Admin corrected a record, so a quietly changed name reaches the booking export without anyone above the accommodation team noticing — an audit view or a notification would close that loop.

```ts
export const listDelegateCorrections = query({
  args: { sessionToken: sessionTokenValidator, limit: v.optional(v.number()) },
  handler: async (ctx, args) => {
    await requireRole(ctx, args.sessionToken, ["admin"]);

    const corrections = (await ctx.db.query("agcSubstitutions").collect())
      .filter((row) => row.actorAdminEmail !== undefined)
      .sort((a, b) => b.createdAt - a.createdAt)

    // Staff accounts are few; the role is what tells a super admin which team
    // made the change, so it is resolved by email rather than left implicit.
    const roleByEmail = new Map(
      (await ctx.db.query("users").collect()).map((u) => [
        u.email.toLowerCase(),
        u.role,

    );

    return corrections.map((row) => {
      const guest = guests.get(row.guestId);
      return {
        _id: row._id,
        createdAt: row.createdAt,
        previousFirstName: row.previousFirstName,
        previousLastName: row.previousLastName,
        previousGender: row.previousGender,
        newFirstName: row.newFirstName,
        newLastName: row.newLastName,
        newGender: row.newGender,
        reason: row.reason ?? null,
        actorEmail: row.actorAdminEmail ?? "",
        /** Null when the account has since been removed. */
        actorRole: roleByEmail.get((row.actorAdminEmail ?? "").toLowerCase()) ?? null,
        /** Name on the guest record now, which later corrections may have moved on. */
        guestName: guest ? `${guest.firstName} ${guest.lastName}`.trim() : null,
```

export const listDelegateCorrections = query({
  args: { sessionToken: sessionTokenValidator, limit: v.optional(v.number()) },
  handler: async (ctx, args) => {
    await requireRole(ctx, args.sessionToken, ["admin"]);

    const corrections = (await ctx.db.query("agcSubstitutions").collect())

import { useQuery } from "convex/react";
import { History } from "lucide-react";
import { api } from "@convex/_generated/api";
import {
  useAdminSession,
  useSessionArgs,
} from "@/components/admin/AdminSessionProvider";
import { Card, CardContent } from "@/components/ui/card";
import { Skeleton } from "@/components/ui/skeleton";
import {
  Table,
  TableBody,
  TableCell,
  TableHead,
  TableHeader,
  TableRow,
} from "@/components/ui/table";
import { ROLE_LABELS, type StaffRole } from "@/lib/adminRoles";

/**
 * Delegate corrections — the audit area's view of the name and gender changes
 * made on locked reservations.
 *
 * A rep can only substitute while a booking is still theirs to change, so once a
 * reservation is confirmed a correction happens in the console: at the desk, in
 * the review queue or on the bookings list. This panel is where a super admin
 * sees that set — who changed what, what the old details were, and the reason
 * they gave — without reading the raw audit log line by line.
 *
 * A rep's own substitution while the booking was still open is recorded on the
 * booking and is deliberately not listed: it needed no review to begin with.
 */

type CorrectionRow = {
  _id: string;
  createdAt: number;
  previousFirstName: string;
  previousLastName: string;
  previousGender: string;
  newFirstName: string;
  newLastName: string;
  newGender: string;
  reason: string | null;
  actorEmail: string;
  actorRole: string | null;
  bookingRef: string | null;
};

function formatDateTime(ts: number) {
  return new Date(ts).toLocaleString(undefined, {
    year: "numeric",
    month: "short",
    day: "numeric",
    hour: "2-digit",
    minute: "2-digit",
  });
}

function roleLabel(role: string | null): string {
  if (!role) return "account removed";
  return ROLE_LABELS[role as StaffRole] ?? role;
}

export function DelegateCorrectionsPanel() {
  const { user } = useAdminSession();
  const sessionArgs = useSessionArgs();
  // The audit area also admits finance, who hold a read-only financial view, so
  // the panel stays with the super admin the query answers to.
  const isSuperAdmin = user?.role === "admin";
  const corrections = useQuery(
    api.admin.listDelegateCorrections,
    isSuperAdmin ? sessionArgs : "skip",
  );

  if (!isSuperAdmin) return null;

  const rows = (corrections ?? []) as CorrectionRow[];

  return (
    <Card>
      <CardContent className="p-0">
        <div className="flex flex-wrap items-start gap-2 border-b px-4 py-3">
          <History className="mt-0.5 size-4 shrink-0 text-muted-foreground" />
          <div className="min-w-0 flex-1">
            <p className="text-sm font-semibold">
              Delegate corrections
              {corrections !== undefined && rows.length > 0 && (
                <span className="ml-2 rounded-full border px-2 py-0.5 text-xs font-normal text-muted-foreground">
                  {rows.length}
                </span>
              )}
            </p>
            <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">
              Names and genders changed on a confirmed reservation by an admin or
              the Accommodation Admin, with the details each change replaced and
              the reason given. A rep's own substitution, made while the
              booking was still open, is recorded on the booking and not listed
              here.
            </p>
          </div>
        </div>

        {corrections === undefined ? (
          <div className="p-4">
            <Skeleton className="h-24 w-full" />
          </div>
        ) : (
          <div className="overflow-x-auto">
            <Table>
              <TableHeader>
                <TableRow className="hover:bg-transparent">
                  <TableHead>When</TableHead>
                  <TableHead>Changed by</TableHead>
                  <TableHead>Was</TableHead>
                  <TableHead>Now</TableHead>
                  <TableHead>Reason</TableHead>
                </TableRow>
              </TableHeader>
              <TableBody>
                {rows.length === 0 ? (
                  <TableRow>
                    <TableCell
                      colSpan={5}
                      className="py-10 text-center text-sm text-muted-foreground"
                    >
                      No delegate has been corrected from the console yet — a
                      name or gender changed at the desk, in the review queue or
                      on a booking appears here with its reason.
                    </TableCell>
                  </TableRow>
                ) : (
                  rows.map((row) => (
                    <TableRow key={row._id}>
                      <TableCell className="align-top text-xs text-muted-foreground">
                        {formatDateTime(row.createdAt)}
                      </TableCell>
                      <TableCell className="align-top text-sm">
                        {row.actorEmail}
                        <span className="mt-0.5 block text-xs text-muted-foreground">
                          {roleLabel(row.actorRole)}
                        </span>
                      </TableCell>
                      <TableCell className="align-top text-sm">
                        {`${row.previousFirstName} ${row.previousLastName}`}
                        <span className="mt-0.5 block text-xs capitalize text-muted-foreground">
                          {row.previousGender}
                        </span>
                      </TableCell>
                      <TableCell className="align-top text-sm font-medium">
                        {`${row.newFirstName} ${row.newLastName}`}
                        <span className="mt-0.5 block text-xs font-normal capitalize text-muted-foreground">
                          {row.newGender}
                        </span>
                      </TableCell>
                      <TableCell className="max-w-72 whitespace-normal align-top text-sm">
                        {row.reason ?? "—"}
                        {row.bookingRef && (
                          <span className="mt-0.5 block text-xs text-muted-foreground">
                            Booking ref {row.bookingRef}
                          </span>
                        )}
                      </TableCell>
                    </TableRow>
                  ))
                )}
              </TableBody>
            </Table>
          </div>
        )}
      </CardContent>
    </Card>
  );
}

**What the audit area shows now.** The page leads with a **Delegate corrections** panel above the raw audit table: one row per correction made in the console, newest first, with When, **Changed by** (email plus the team they belong to), **Was**, **Now**, and the **Reason** — the booking reference sits under the reason. So a super admin sees `Guest1 Mensah · male → Ama Boateng · female`, that it was done by `accommodation@example.com · Accommodation`, and why, without scanning audit lines.

**Where the data comes from, and why.** I read the correction history rather than the audit log: the log's summary is a formatted sentence, while `agcSubstitutions` carries the previous and new name and gender as separate fields, plus the reason. The set is exactly the rows with an acting staff member — a rep's own substitution, made while the booking was still theirs to change, has no staff actor and is excluded, which is the honest boundary since those never needed a review. The panel says that in its own copy rather than leaving the omission to be discovered. The actor's role isn't stored on the row, so [listDelegateCorrections](convex/admin.ts#L254) resolves it from the acting account; a role of `null` means the account has since been removed, and the panel says "account removed" rather than inventing a team.

**Two judgement calls worth your eye.** The panel is gated to the `admin` role, matching the audit queries — not to finance, who can reach the audit area for the financial view and would get `Unauthorized` from an admin-only query. And I deliberately list super admins' corrections alongside the accommodation team's, labelled by role; the ask was to see what the accommodation team changed, and showing only them would have hidden the admin's own changes from the same screen.

**One test-infra fix along the way.** `tests/testUtils.ts` never listed `convex/admin.ts` in its module map — no test had touched that module — so the new test failed with "Could not find module for: admin" until I added it. That's a one-line addition to the list whose own comment says it exists to keep future tests working.

The new test in [agcPhase2.test.ts](tests/agcPhase2.test.ts#L1934) covers the empty list, the rep substitution being excluded, both a super admin's and an Accommodation Admin's correction appearing with resolved roles and reasons, newest-first ordering, and the desk role being refused the query.

**Limitations.** Nothing is push-notified: a correction shows up on this screen but nobody is alerted to it, so a super admin has to look. There's no filter or date range yet — the list is capped at the 100 most recent corrections, which is the right size for a conference but worth knowing if corrections ever run much higher. And as before, no browser pass — the console needs staff credentials — so the panel is covered by type checks, tests and build rather than by eye.

+import { ROLE_LABELS, type StaffRole } from "@/lib/adminRoles";
+
+/**
+ * Delegate corrections — the audit area's view of the name and gender changes
+ * made on locked reservations.
+ *
+ * A rep can only substitute while a booking is still theirs to change, so once a
+ * reservation is confirmed a correction happens in the console: at the desk, in
+ * the review queue or on the bookings list. This panel is where a super admin
+ * sees that set — who changed what, what the old details were, and the reason
+ * they gave — without reading the raw audit log line by line.
+ *
+ * A rep's own substitution while the booking was still open is recorded on the
+ * booking and is deliberately not listed: it needed no review to begin with.
+ */
+
+type CorrectionRow = {
+  _id: string;
+  createdAt: number;
+  previousFirstName: string;
+  previousLastName: string;
+  previousGender: string;
+  newFirstName: string;
+  newLastName: string;
+  newGender: string;
+  reason: string | null;
+  actorEmail: string;
+  actorRole: string | null;
+  bookingRef: string | null;
+};
+
+function formatDateTime(ts: number) {
+  return new Date(ts).toLocaleString(undefined, {
+    year: "numeric",
+    month: "short",
+    day: "numeric",
+    hour: "2-digit",
+    minute: "2-digit",
+  });
+}
+
+function roleLabel(role: string | null): string {
+  if (!role) return "account removed";
+  return ROLE_LABELS[role as StaffRole] ?? role;
+}
+
+export function DelegateCorrectionsPanel() {
+  const { user } = useAdminSession();
+  const sessionArgs = useSessionArgs();
+  // The audit area also admits finance, who hold a read-only financial view, so
+  // the panel stays with the super admin the query answers to.
+  const isSuperAdmin = user?.role === "admin";
+  const corrections = useQuery(
+    api.admin.listDelegateCorrections,
+    isSuperAdmin ? sessionArgs : "skip",
+  );
+
+  if (!isSuperAdmin) return null;
+
+  const rows = (corrections ?? []) as CorrectionRow[];
+

+          <div className="min-w-0 flex-1">
+            <p className="text-sm font-semibold">
+              Delegate corrections
+              {corrections !== undefined && rows.length > 0 && (
+                <span className="ml-2 rounded-full border px-2 py-0.5 text-xs font-normal text-muted-foreground">
