+test("the audit area lists console delegate corrections with who made them and why", async () => {
+  const t = createTestConvex();
+  const admin = await seedStaff(t, "admin");
+  const accommodation = await seedStaff(t, "accommodation");
+  const desk = await seedStaff(t, "checkin");
+  const booking = await seedConfirmedBooking(t, {
+    accommodationType: "hostel",
+    gender: "male",
+    count: 2,
+  });
+  const [firstGuest, secondGuest] = booking.guestIds as Id<"agcGuests">[];
+
+  // A rep's own substitution, made while the booking was still theirs to change,
+  // is not a console correction — no acting staff member on the row — so it must
+  // not appear on the audit screen.
+  await t.run(async (ctx) => {
+    await ctx.db.insert("agcSubstitutions", {
+      bookingId: booking.bookingId,
+      guestId: secondGuest,
+      previousFirstName: "Guest1",
+      previousLastName: "Mensah",
+      previousGender: "male",
+      previousType: "hostel",
+      newFirstName: "Yaw",
+      newLastName: "Mensah",
+      newGender: "male",
+      newType: "hostel",
+      overrideByAdmin: false,
+      actorRepId: booking.repId,
+      reason: "Delegate swapped before the deadline",
+      createdAt: 500,
+    });
+  });
+
+  // Nothing to review yet, and that is an empty list rather than an error.
+  let rows = await t.query(api.admin.listDelegateCorrections, {
+    sessionToken: admin.token,
+  });
+  expect(rows).toEqual([]);
+
+  // Two corrections on a locked reservation: the super admin's and the
+  // Accommodation Admin's. Both are the set this screen exists to show.
+  await t.mutation(api.agcAdminData.correctBookingGuest, {
+    sessionToken: admin.token,
+    guestId: firstGuest,
+    firstName: "Kofi",
+    lastName: "Boateng",
+    gender: "male",
+    reason: "Original delegate could not travel",
+  });
+  await t.mutation(api.agcAdminData.correctBookingGuest, {
+    sessionToken: accommodation.token,
+    guestId: secondGuest,
+    firstName: "Ama",
+    lastName: "Boateng",
+    gender: "female",
+    reason: "Gender recorded in error at registration",
+  });
+
+  rows = await t.query(api.admin.listDelegateCorrections, {
+    sessionToken: admin.token,
+  });
+  expect(rows).toHaveLength(2);
+
+  // Newest first: pin the two rows to known times so the order does not depend
+  // on the millisecond the two mutations happened to land in.
+  const adminRow = rows.find((row) => row.newFirstName === "Kofi");
+  const accommodationRow = rows.find((row) => row.newFirstName === "Ama");
+  expect(adminRow).toBeTruthy();
+  expect(accommodationRow).toBeTruthy();
+  await t.run(async (ctx) => {
+    await ctx.db.patch(adminRow!._id, { createdAt: 1_000 });
+    await ctx.db.patch(accommodationRow!._id, { createdAt: 2_000 });
+  });
+  rows = await t.query(api.admin.listDelegateCorrections, {
+    sessionToken: admin.token,
+  });
+  expect(rows.map((row) => row.newFirstName)).toEqual(["Ama", "Kofi"]);
+
+  // Each row says what was replaced, who did it — role included, since that is
+  // what tells a super admin which team moved the delegate — and the reason.
+  expect(rows[0]).toMatchObject({
+    previousFirstName: "Guest1",
+    previousLastName: "Mensah",
+    previousGender: "male",
+    newFirstName: "Ama",
+    newLastName: "Boateng",
+    newGender: "female",
+    reason: "Gender recorded in error at registration",
+    actorEmail: "accommodation@example.com",
+    actorRole: "accommodation",
+    bookingRef: "AGC-BK-0001",
+  });
+  expect(rows[1]).toMatchObject({
+    previousFirstName: "Guest0",
+    newFirstName: "Kofi",
+    reason: "Original delegate could not travel",
+    actorEmail: "admin@example.com",
+    actorRole: "admin",
+  });
+
+  // Reading the corrections is the super admin's view, not the desk's.
+  await expect(() =>
+    t.query(api.admin.listDelegateCorrections, { sessionToken: desk.token }),
+  ).rejects.toThrow(/Unauthorized/);
+
+  // The audit log itself still carries every correction as its own event.
+  const audit = await t.run(async (ctx) =>
+    (await ctx.db.query("auditLogs").collect()).filter(
+      (log) => log.action === "agc_guest.corrected",
+    ),
+  );
+  expect(audit).toHaveLength(2);
+});

```ts
export const listDelegateCorrections = query({
  args: {
    sessionToken: sessionTokenValidator,
    limit: v.optional(v.number()),
    /** Only corrections made by this staff account (case-insensitive email). */
    actorEmail: v.optional(v.string()),
    /** Inclusive epoch-ms bounds on when the correction was made. */
    from: v.optional(v.number()),
    to: v.optional(v.number()),
  },
  handler: async (ctx, args) => {
    await requireRole(ctx, args.sessionToken, ["admin"]);

    const all = (await ctx.db.query("agcSubstitutions").collect()).filter(
      (row): row is typeof row & { actorAdminEmail: string } =>
        row.actorAdminEmail !== undefined,
    );
    const roleByEmail = new Map(...users...);
    const actorOf = (email: string) => roleByEmail.get(email.toLowerCase()) ?? null;

    // The filter options come from the corrections themselves, so a super admin
    // picks from the people who have actually changed a delegate.
    const actors = [...all.reduce((map, row) => {...}, new Map<string, number>())]
      .map(([email, count]) => ({ email, count, role: actorOf(email) }))
      .sort((a, b) => b.count - a.count || a.email.localeCompare(b.email));

    const wanted = args.actorEmail?.trim().toLowerCase();
    const filtered = all
      .filter((row) => !wanted || row.actorAdminEmail.toLowerCase() === wanted)
      .filter((row) => args.from === undefined || row.createdAt >= args.from)
      .filter((row) => args.to === undefined || row.createdAt <= args.to)
      .sort((a, b) => b.createdAt - a.createdAt);

    const bookingById = ...;

    return {
      total: all.length,
      actors,
      rows: filtered.slice(0, args.limit ?? 100).map(...),
    };
  },
});
```

Both done and pushed as **32cbbfd** on `origin/master` (`6733462..32cbbfd`, working tree clean).

**Corrections filtering.** The panel now has a filter bar: **Changed by** (a dropdown of the people who have actually corrected a delegate, each labelled with their team and how many they made), and **From** / **To** date pickers, with a Clear link once anything is set. The count beside the heading reads `3 of 12` while a filter is on, so it's obvious the view is narrowed, and the empty state says "no correction matches these filters — clear them to see all 12" rather than pretending nothing ever happened.

I put the filtering in [the query](convex/admin.ts#L254) rather than over the loaded page: the list is capped at 100 rows, so filtering in the browser would silently hide older corrections that match. The dates are converted to epoch bounds in your own timezone (`from` = start of the picked day, `to` = end of it), so both days named by the range are included — the test pins that boundary. The dropdown options come from the data, so it never offers a person who has corrected nobody, and the email match is case-insensitive.

**Desk sheet.** The check-in table now scrolls inside its own 60vh area with the header pinned (`sticky top-0` with a bottom rule), so a long roster no longer pushes the record card and the desk tools down the page. The record card sticks below the console header (`lg:top-16` — the 4rem offset the rooms grid, runbook and desk pages already use; it was `lg:top-20` before) and scrolls inside itself when the actions stack taller than the window, so the room, payment and key stay beside the row you're working on. I reused the pattern already in the accommodation portal's table rather than inventing one.

**One thing I backed out.** I first kept the previous results on screen while a filter round-trips, using a ref — the project's `react-hooks/refs` lint rule rejects reading a ref during render, and the test for that pattern is a fight I'd rather not pick for polish. So the panel shows its loading skeleton briefly when you change a filter or pick a date. If that flicker bothers you in practice, the fix is a `useState` "previous result" holder, which the linter does allow.

**Verified.** `npx tsc --noEmit` ✓, `npm run lint` ✓ 0 problems, `npx vitest run` **240/240** ✓, `npm run build` ✓. The corrections test now also checks the actor list (email, team, count), filtering by a differently-cased actor email, both ends of an inclusive date range, a range that excludes everything, and the two filters combined — and confirms the filtered response still reports the unfiltered total.

**Limitations.** Still no browser pass — the console needs staff credentials and you have your own dev server — so the sticky scroll behaviour is the one thing here that wants your eyes: I verified the classes match the repo's existing sticky patterns and that the build compiles, but I haven't watched it scroll. Filtering is by person, not by team as such; a team-level filter would be a short addition if "show me everything Accommodation did" is what you actually reach for.

+test("the audit area lists console delegate corrections with who made them and why", async () => {
+  const t = createTestConvex();
+  const admin = await seedStaff(t, "admin");
+  const accommodation = await seedStaff(t, "accommodation");
+  const desk = await seedStaff(t, "checkin");
+  const booking = await seedConfirmedBooking(t, {
+    accommodationType: "hostel",
+    gender: "male",
+    count: 2,
+  });
+  const [firstGuest, secondGuest] = booking.guestIds as Id<"agcGuests">[];
+
+  // A rep's own substitution, made while the booking was still theirs to change,
+  // is not a console correction — no acting staff member on the row — so it must
+  // not appear on the audit screen.
+  await t.run(async (ctx) => {
+    await ctx.db.insert("agcSubstitutions", {
+      bookingId: booking.bookingId,
+      guestId: secondGuest,
+      previousFirstName: "Guest1",
+      previousLastName: "Mensah",
+      previousGender: "male",
+      previousType: "hostel",
+      newFirstName: "Yaw",
+      newLastName: "Mensah",
+      newGender: "male",
+      newType: "hostel",
+      overrideByAdmin: false,
+      actorRepId: booking.repId,
+      reason: "Delegate swapped before the deadline",
+      createdAt: 500,
+    });
+  });
+
+  // Nothing to review yet, and that is an empty list rather than an error.
+  let result = await t.query(api.admin.listDelegateCorrections, {
+    sessionToken: admin.token,
+  });
+  expect(result.rows).toEqual([]);
+  expect(result.total).toBe(0);
+  expect(result.actors).toEqual([]);
+
+  // Two corrections on a locked reservation: the super admin's and the
+  // Accommodation Admin's. Both are the set this screen exists to show.
+  await t.mutation(api.agcAdminData.correctBookingGuest, {
+    sessionToken: admin.token,
+    guestId: firstGuest,
+    firstName: "Kofi",
+    lastName: "Boateng",
+    gender: "male",
+    reason: "Original delegate could not travel",
+  });
+  await t.mutation(api.agcAdminData.correctBookingGuest, {
+    sessionToken: accommodation.token,
+    guestId: secondGuest,
+    firstName: "Ama",
+    lastName: "Boateng",
+    gender: "female",
+    reason: "Gender recorded in error at registration",
+  });
+
+  result = await t.query(api.admin.listDelegateCorrections, {
+    sessionToken: admin.token,
+  });
+  expect(result.total).toBe(2);
+  expect(result.rows).toHaveLength(2);
+  // The filter offers the people who have actually made a correction, with how
+  // many each of them made and the team they belong to.
+  expect(result.actors.map((actor) => actor.email).sort()).toEqual([
+    "accommodation@example.com",
+    "admin@example.com",
+  ]);
+  expect(
+    result.actors.find((actor) => actor.email === "accommodation@example.com"),
+  ).toMatchObject({ role: "accommodation", count: 1 });
+
+  // Newest first: pin the two rows to known times so the order does not depend
+  // on the millisecond the two mutations happened to land in.
+  const adminRow = result.rows.find((row) => row.newFirstName === "Kofi");
+  const accommodationRow = result.rows.find((row) => row.newFirstName === "Ama");
+  expect(adminRow).toBeTruthy();
+  expect(accommodationRow).toBeTruthy();
+  await t.run(async (ctx) => {
+    await ctx.db.patch(adminRow!._id, { createdAt: 1_000 });
+    await ctx.db.patch(accommodationRow!._id, { createdAt: 2_000 });
+  });
+  result = await t.query(api.admin.listDelegateCorrections, {
+    sessionToken: admin.token,
+  });
+  expect(result.rows.map((row) => row.newFirstName)).toEqual(["Ama", "Kofi"]);
+
+  // Each row says what was replaced, who did it — role included, since that is
+  // what tells a super admin which team moved the delegate — and the reason.
+  expect(result.rows[0]).toMatchObject({
+    previousFirstName: "Guest1",
+    previousLastName: "Mensah",
+    previousGender: "male",
+    newFirstName: "Ama",
+    newLastName: "Boateng",
+    newGender: "female",
+    reason: "Gender recorded in error at registration",
+    actorEmail: "accommodation@example.com",
+    actorRole: "accommodation",
+    bookingRef: "AGC-BK-0001",
+  });
+  expect(result.rows[1]).toMatchObject({
+    previousFirstName: "Guest0",
+    newFirstName: "Kofi",
+    reason: "Original delegate could not travel",
+    actorEmail: "admin@example.com",
+    actorRole: "admin",
+  });
+
+  // Filtering by who made the change keeps the other corrections out, while the
+  // actor list still offers everyone who has one — so the reviewer can widen
+  // again without clearing the filter and starting over.
+  const byAccommodation = await t.query(api.admin.listDelegateCorrections, {
+    sessionToken: admin.token,
+    actorEmail: "ACCOMMODATION@example.com",
+  });
+  expect(byAccommodation.rows.map((row) => row.newFirstName)).toEqual(["Ama"]);
+  expect(byAccommodation.total).toBe(2);
+  expect(byAccommodation.actors).toHaveLength(2);
+
+  // The date range is inclusive of both days it names, in the viewer's own day
+  // boundaries (the panel sends epoch bounds for the picked dates).
+  const onTheDay = await t.query(api.admin.listDelegateCorrections, {
+    sessionToken: admin.token,
+    from: 2_000,
+    to: 2_000,
+  });
+  expect(onTheDay.rows.map((row) => row.newFirstName)).toEqual(["Ama"]);
+  const afterTheDay = await t.query(api.admin.listDelegateCorrections, {
+    sessionToken: admin.token,
+    from: 2_001,
+  });
+  expect(afterTheDay.rows).toEqual([]);
+  const beforeBoth = await t.query(api.admin.listDelegateCorrections, {
+    sessionToken: admin.token,
+    to: 999,
+  });
+  expect(beforeBoth.rows).toEqual([]);
+  const bothFilters = await t.query(api.admin.listDelegateCorrections, {
+    sessionToken: admin.token,
+    actorEmail: "admin@example.com",
+    from: 1_000,
+    to: 1_000,
+  });
+  expect(bothFilters.rows.map((row) => row.newFirstName)).toEqual(["Kofi"]);
+
+  // Reading the corrections is the super admin's view, not the desk's.
+  await expect(() =>
+    t.query(api.admin.listDelegateCorrections, { sessionToken: desk.token }),
+  ).rejects.toThrow(/Unauthorized/);
+
+  // The audit log itself still carries every correction as its own event.
+  const audit = await t.run(async (ctx) =>
+    (await ctx.db.query("auditLogs").collect()).filter(

/**

 *
 * A physical problem stays with the room, not with a delegate: "the toilet is

const ROOM_FLAG_ROLES = ["admin", "accommodation", "room_assignment", "checkin"] as const;

const ROOM_FLAG_RESOLVE_ROLES = ["admin", "accommodation"] as const;

 * read without walking the list again. `includeFixed` is for the history view;
 * the grid only wants what is still wrong.

  handler: async (ctx, args) => {
    const actor = await requireRole(ctx, args.sessionToken, [...ROOM_FLAG_RESOLVE_ROLES]);
    const issue = await ctx.db.get(args.issueId);
    if (!issue) throw new ConvexError("That room flag no longer exists");
    if (issue.resolvedAt) {

export const checkOutGuest = mutation({","newString":"/**
 * Desk bulk check-in: tick several ready delegates anywhere on the sheet and
 * check them in together. Unlike group check-in (§13) the selection may span
 * hubs, because the desk ticks whoever is standing in front of it.
 *
 * Each delegate still goes through the single check-in rules — assignment,
 * payment gate, duplicate guard, key handling — and one rejection never
 * blocks the rest. The per-delegate outcomes come back for the toast.
 */
export const checkInBatch = mutation({
  args: {
    sessionToken: v.string(),
    location: v.string(),
    guests: v.array(
      v.object({
        guestId: v.id("agcGuests"),
        override: v.optional(v.object({ reason: v.string() })),
        keyRecipientName: v.optional(v.string()),
      }),
    ),
  },
  handler: async (ctx, args): Promise<{
    checkedInCount: number;
    rejectedCount: number;
    results: GroupArrivalResult[];
  }> => {
    const user = await requireRole(ctx, args.sessionToken, [...CHECKIN_ROLES]);
    if (args.guests.length === 0) {
      throw new ConvexError("Tick at least one delegate to check in");
    }
    if (args.guests.length > 100) {
      throw new ConvexError("Check in at most 100 delegates at a time");
    }
    const seen = new Set<string>();
    for (const entry of args.guests) {
      if (seen.has(entry.guestId)) {
        throw new ConvexError("The same delegate was ticked twice");
      }
      seen.add(entry.guestId);
    }

    const actor: CheckinActor = {
      userId: user._id,
      email: user.email,
      role: user.role,
    };
    const results: GroupArrivalResult[] = [];
    for (const entry of args.guests) {
      try {
        const checkIn = await performCheckIn(ctx, actor, {
          guestId: entry.guestId,
          location: args.location,
          override: entry.override,
          keyRecipientName: entry.keyRecipientName,
        });
        results.push({
          guestId: entry.guestId,
          status: "checked_in",
          keyIssued: checkIn.keyIssued,
          keysAlreadyIssuedTo: checkIn.keysAlreadyIssuedTo,
        });
      } catch (err) {
        results.push({
          guestId: entry.guestId,
          status: "rejected",
          reason: err instanceof Error ? err.message : "check-in failed",
        });
      }
    }
    const checkedInCount = results.filter((r) => r.status === "checked_in").length;
    const rejectedCount = results.filter((r) => r.status === "rejected").length;

    await writeAuditLog(ctx, {
      actorUserId: user._id,
      actorEmail: user.email,
      action: "agc_checkin.desk_batch",
      entityType: "agcCheckIns",
      summary: `Desk bulk check-in: ${checkedInCount} checked in, ${rejectedCount} rejected of ${args.guests.length} ticked by ${user.email}`,
      metadata: {
        results: results.map((r) =>
          r.status === "rejected" ? { guestId: r.guestId, reason: r.reason } : { guestId: r.guestId },
        ),
      },
    });

    return { checkedInCount, rejectedCount, results };
  },
});

On [the rooms screen](src/components/admin/agc/RoomsTab.tsx) it now sits disabled with a small "Off — enable in Settings → Operations" note beside it. A new switch in [Settings → Operational controls](src/components/admin/agc/AgcSettingsManager.tsx) arms it, and the switch is audit-logged. The arrival desk shows eight skeleton rows in the sheet. Empty states now only appear when a query has genuinely answered with nothing.

**Assign-to-room card follows the filters.** A room-type filter narrows the card to that type. A hub filter narrows it to the accommodation types that hub's waiting delegates actually booked, since a room of another type could never take them. The card says which filters are applying, offers "Show all rooms", and changing a filter releases any previously picked room so the Assign button can't point at a room that is no longer visible.

## The audit, item by item

| # | Capability | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Do what other roles do, and more | Could not open the rooms console at all; no room CRUD, import, publish, hold or fault powers | Matches check-in staff at the desk and accommodation staff on the room inventory, corrections and flags. Deliberately **not** payments: bookings review, pools, POA and finance stay with those roles |
| 2 | Change names / gender | Admin + accommodation only | Room-assignment staff too, server-side and in the desk's "Correct name / gender" |
| 3 | Reserve rooms and release them | Did not exist | New room hold with a required reason, releasable any time; a held room is refused by every assignment path |
| 4 | See the arrival desk and do everything there | Page accessible, but overrides, corrections, flag-clearing and conflict resolution were approver-only | All desk decisions now open to the role |
| 5 | Mark a room faulty and take it out of inventory | Faults were notes only; the room stayed assignable | "Take this room out of inventory" on the flag form — blocked rooms are refused by assignment, excluded from auto-assign and the room pickers, and counted as faulty |
| 6 | Resolve faults and release back into inventory | Resolving admin/accommodation only, and changed nothing | Room-assignment staff can resolve; fixing the last blocking fault returns the room to service automatically |
| 7 | Clear any flag | Approver roles only | Room-assignment staff can clear review flags from the desk or the queue |
| 8 | Assign, unassign, swap | Server allowed it, but the screen was unreachable | Console access added; swaps and unassigns work from the rooms page and the desk |
| 9 | Dashboard numbers | None | New strip: available beds/rooms, reserved, faulty, occupied, awaiting a room, keys out/returned |
| 10 | Undo a check-in | Approver-only | "Correct check-in" available, with the reason recorded |
| 11 | Add a last-minute delegate | Did not exist | "Add last-minute delegate" on the rooms page creates a confirmed zero-value booking + guest, immediately roomable and check-in ready |
| 12 | See and resolve failed offline actions | Resolve was approver-only | Visible and resolvable; I also fixed a real bug where a rejected resolution stayed in the queue forever |

## Room flags at the desk

The arrival sheet now marks any delegate whose room has an open fault with a red **Faulty** chip, the record card lists every open fault on that room (category and note, with "out of inventory" when it blocks), and the confirm-arrival dialog repeats the warning so staff see it *before* checking someone in. Check-in is not blocked — the delegate may already be living there — but the fault is shown. Faults come from the same records the rooms page maintains.

## Things worth knowing

- **Payments boundary.** "Do what the other roles can do and more" was read as operational authority (rooms + desk + corrections + flags + conflicts), not financial authority. Room-assignment staff can authorize a desk payment override, but cannot review bookings, confirm POA payments, move pool totals or open Settings. If the client actually wants the financial role too, that's a separate, deliberate widening.
- **Walk-in bookings bypass the pool ledger.** A volunteer never bought a pool bed; the physical room is what constrains them. This is documented in the mutation. The booking is attributed to the hub's first rep (the schema requires a rep), with the acting staff member named in the audit log.
- **Auto-assign** remains opt-in from Settings, and now also skips held and faulty rooms.

**On the check-in desk card, three actions now sit under the delegate's details** — everything else on the page is untouched: the same search, filters, sheet, bulk check-in and record actions are all still where they were.

- **Issue key** appears for a checked-in delegate whose keyed room has no key out (Pending, or Returned after it came back to the drawer). It asks who physically holds it, pre-filled with the delegate's name. This matters because the key is normally collected during the check-in dialog; if the delegate settles in first and comes back for the key, the desk can record the hand-over without re-running the arrival. One key stays open per room — if it is already out with someone, the desk is told who and must mark it returned or replace it first.
- **Mark key returned** is unchanged and sits in the same place.
- **Undo check-in** is the new destructive-style action for admins, the Accommodation Admin and room-assignment staff, with a required reason. It removes the arrival, so the delegate drops back to *Not Arrived* and can be checked in again properly (wrong person at the counter, wrong room). The reason and a full snapshot of the arrival — room, checked-in time, who did it, location, any payment override — go to the audit log, since the row itself is gone. A key recorded at that check-in is deliberately **not** silently erased: the desk is told who still holds it, because the key physically left the drawer and has to come back.

The old "the key is issued in the check-in step" hint now only shows before arrival, so a checked-in delegate with a pending key sees the button instead of a contradiction.

**Room cards on the rooms screen now carry a folded fault history.** Each card with past repairs has a *Fault history (n)* line under its open problems; opening it lists the six most recent fixed faults with category, note, fix date, who fixed it and any resolution note, plus a count of older ones. Because a room that keeps breaking is the real signal, a category that appears more than once is named right in the collapsed line — *recurring: Toilet ×3* — so it reads at a glance without expanding anything. Open faults still show loudly in red as before; only resolved ones fold into the history. Nothing else on the card or the screen changed.

 * Desk check-ins taken while the building's station is offline (Phase 2 §19).
 *
 * The queue lives on the device, not the server — that is the whole point of a
 * dead zone. Each entry carries the transaction id the server dedupes on, so a
 * replay that is repeated (tap twice, tab reopened) still checks a delegate in
 * once. Nothing here talks to Convex: the desk decides when to push, and the
 * server decides whether each transaction applies or needs review.
 */

export type QueuedDeskCheckIn = {
  /** Client-generated id; the server stores a transaction once per id. */
  txId: string;
  guestId: string;
  /** Kept for the desk's own list — the server resolves the real record. */
  guestName: string;
  /** Building whose designated station may queue this transaction. */
  building: string;
  /** Desk location recorded on the arrival. */
  location: string;
  /** Who takes the key, for key-tracked rooms. */
  keyRecipientName?: string;
  originalAt: number;
};

/** The slice of Storage the queue needs, so tests can pass a plain object. */
export type QueueStorage = {
  getItem(key: string): string | null;
  setItem(key: string, value: string): void;
  removeItem(key: string): void;
};

export const QUEUE_STORAGE_KEY = "homecoming-desk-offline-checkins-v1";

function resolveStorage(storage?: QueueStorage | null): QueueStorage | null {
  i [… 513 characters omitted] y.guestId === "string" &&
    entry.guestId.length > 0 &&
    typeof entry.building === "string" &&
    typeof entry.location === "string" &&
    typeof entry.originalAt === "number"
  );
}

/** This device's queue, oldest first. Unreadable storage reads as empty. */
export function loadQueuedCheckIns(
  storage?: QueueStorage | null,
): QueuedDeskCheckIn[] {
  const store = resolveStorage(storage);
  if (!store) return [];
  try {
    const raw = store.getItem(QUEUE_STORAGE_KEY);
    if (!raw) return [];
    const parsed = JSON.parse(raw) as unknown;
    if (!Array.isArray(parsed)) return [];
    return parsed.filter(isEntry).sort((a, b) => a.originalAt - b.originalAt);
  } catch {
    return [];
  }
}

function write(rows: QueuedDeskCheckIn[], storage?: QueueStorage | null) {
  const store = resolveStorage(storage);
  if (!store) return rows;
  try {
    store.setItem(QUEUE_STORAGE_KEY, JSON.stringify(rows));
  } catch {
    // Quota or private mode — the desk keeps its in-memory copy.
  }
  return rows;
}

/** Add one check-in to the device queue, replacing any entry for that guest. */
export function enqueueCheckIn(
  entry: QueuedDeskCheckIn,
  storage?: QueueStorage | null,
): QueuedDeskCheckIn[] {
  // One queued arrival per delegate: a second tap must not store a second tx.
  const rows = loadQueuedCheckIns(storage).filter(
    (row) => row.guestId !== entry.guestId,
  );
  rows.push(entry);
  return write(
    rows.sort((a, b) => a.originalAt - b.originalAt),
    storage,
  );
}

/** Drop entries the server has taken (applied, conflict or rejected). */
export function removeQueuedCheckIns(
  txIds: string[],
  storage?: QueueStorage | null,
): QueuedDeskCheckIn[] {
  const drop = new Set(txIds);
  const rows = loadQueuedCheckIns(storage).filter((row) => !drop.has(row.txId));
  return write(rows, storage);
}

/** A transaction id the server can dedupe on. */
export function newOfflineTxId(): string {
  if (typeof crypto !== "undefined" && typeof crypto.randomUUID === "function") {
    return crypto.randomUUID();
  }
  // Older browsers without randomUUID still get an id that is unique enough
  // for a desk queue (time + randomness), never reused across devices.
  return `tx-${Date.now().toString(36)}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 10)}`;

function memoryStorage(): QueueStorage {
  const map = new Map<string, string>();
  return {
    getItem: (key) => map.get(key) ?? null,
    setItem: (key, value) => {
      map.set(key, value);
    },
    removeItem: (key) => {
      map.delete(key);
    },
  };

function entry(overrides: Partial<QueuedDeskCheckIn> = {}): QueuedDeskCheckIn {
  return {
    txId: "tx-1",
    guestId: "guest-1",
    guestName: "Ama Mensah",
    building: "Blocks 1–4",
    location: "Blocks 1–4",
    originalAt: 1_000,
    ...overrides,
  };
}

describe("desk offline queue", () => {
  test("keeps queued arrivals oldest first and survives a reload", () => {
    const storage = memoryStorage();
    enqueueCheckIn(entry({ txId: "tx-late", originalAt: 2_000 }), storage);
    enqueueCheckIn(entry({ txId: "tx-early", guestId: "guest-2", originalAt: 1_000 }), storage);

    expect(loadQueuedCheckIns(storage).map((row) => row.txId)).toEqual([
      "tx-early",
      "tx-late",
    ]);
  });

  test("one queued arrival per delegate — a second tap replaces, never doubles", () => {
    const storage = memoryStorage();
    enqueueCheckIn(entry({ txId: "tx-1" }), storage);
    enqueueCheckIn(entry({ txId: "tx-2" }), storage);

    const rows = loadQueuedCheckIns(storage);
    expect(rows).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(rows[0]?.txId).toBe("tx-2");
  });

  test("only the synced transactions leave the queue", () => {
    const storage = memoryStorage();
    enqueueCheckIn(entry({ txId: "tx-1" }), storage);
    enqueueCheckIn(entry({ txId: "tx-2", guestId: "guest-2" }), storage);

    const left = removeQueuedCheckIns(["tx-1"], storage);
    expect(left.map((row) => row.txId)).toEqual(["tx-2"]);
    expect(loadQueuedCheckIns(storage).map((row) => row.txId)).toEqual(["tx-2"]);
  });

  test("unreadable or tampered storage reads as an empty queue", () => {
    const storage = memoryStorage();
    storage.setItem(QUEUE_STORAGE_KEY, "not-json");
    expect(loadQueuedCheckIns(storage)).toEqual([]);

    storage.setItem(
      QUEUE_STORAGE_KEY,
      JSON.stringify([{ txId: "tx-1" }, entry({ txId: "tx-good" })]),
    );
    expect(loadQueuedCheckIns(storage).map((row) => row.txId)).toEqual(["tx-good"]);
  });

  test("missing storage (private mode) never throws and keeps memory in sync", () => {
    const storage = memoryStorage();
    storage.setItem = () => {
      throw new Error("QuotaExceededError");
    };
    expect(() => enqueueCheckIn(entry(), storage)).not.toThrow();
  });

  test("transaction ids are unique", () => {
    const ids = new Set(Array.from({ length: 20 }, () => newOfflineTxId()));
    expect(ids.size).toBe(20);
  });
});

Audited every item against the code, then built only the gaps. Pushed as **2454bd9** (`ed28057..2454bd9`, clean tree).

**Already there — left untouched:** check-in, check-out, issuing and returning keys, flagging a delegate for review, and flagging a room for review (the desk's Out of service panel). The delegate search already matched name, hub, room number, building and booking reference.

**Missing — now added**

1. **Posted to a building.** The users table had a `defaultLocation` field that nothing read or wrote. The Team page now has a **Building** picker per staff member (Central = any), audit-logged and admin-only. A check-in account posted to a building lands on that building's desk, the location pill is locked to it, and the sheet, faults, reserved rooms and room search are all that building's only. Approvers keep the switcher because they cover the whole site.
2. **Check-in while offline.** The server queue existed but no client ever filled it — the panel only synced transactions nobody had queued. There is now a per-device queue: when the station is disconnected (or the connection drops between tap and write), single, bulk and group check-ins are stored on the device instead of failing, the row reads **Queued offline** with a Local badge, and that delegate is blocked from being ticked or checked in again. Reconnecting pushes them automatically, or **Push and sync** does it by hand; the server dedupes on transaction id, so a repeated push can never create two arrivals. Each entry keeps the staff identity that took it, so the audit trail names the right person even if someone else syncs later.
3. **Undo and move for check-in staff.** Undo was admin/accommodation/room-assignment only and the Move button was hidden from check-in staff. Undo (reason required, audit snapshot, delegate back to Not Arrived) is now open to every desk role, and Move is visible to them — the server already allowed room changes for the role.
4. **Reserved rooms on the desk.** A read-only **Reserved rooms** panel in Desk overview & tools lists the room, type, building, the reason and who held it, and says the room team releases it. Reserved rooms remain unavailable for assignment.
5. **Key totals both ways.** The Keys panel header now reads **“Keys — n out · m returned (x key records in total)”** instead of only counting keys out.
6. **Room search.** Searching a room number (or building/type) now shows a strip of matching rooms above the sheet with type, building, occupancy and whether each is reserved or faulty — the only way to find an empty room, since it has no delegate to match.

Runbook updated: the role table, the undo step, offline station behaviour, the reserved-rooms pointer and the room search are covered in both the in-app help and [RUNBOOK-NOV3.md](RUNBOOK-NOV3.md).

No browser pass — the console needs staff credentials.

**Two limits worth knowing:** offline queueing needs a designated station for that building, and only an admin/accommodation/room-assignment account can designate one, so the station must be set up before the dead zone; and a posted check-in station sees only delegates whose room is in its building, so an unassigned delegate will not appear in its sheet by design.

The short answer: yes, but not by "saving the file" somewhere free — someone always hosts the bytes. The win is in **shrinking what you keep, deleting what nothing references, and hosting new uploads on a cheaper/free-tier bucket**. I checked your upload path and the billing numbers before answering.

## What your receipts actually cost

| | Convex file storage | Cloudflare R2 | Backblaze B2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Storage | $0.033/GB-mo (1 GB free) | $0.015/GB-mo (10 GB free) | ~$0.006/GB-mo (10 GB free) |
| Egress | $0.132/GB | free | free (via Cloudflare) |
| Ops | included in call/compute | $4.50/M writes, $0.36/M reads | ~free |

So Convex storage is roughly **2× R2 per GB and the only one that bills you for downloads**. Note the scale though: 3,000 receipts at ~300 KB each is under 1 GB — about **$0.03/month**. If your bill is climbing in a way that hurts, receipts-as-images are unlikely to be the whole story; the likely culprits are PDFs (never compressed), orphaned blobs, and query/compute traffic rather than raw bytes.

**Where to look first:** the console dashboard already computes this from `_storage` — the "File storage · X MB · N files" card shows `gallery · receipts · hero/tours · other`. That "other" count is files **nothing references** — a pure leak counter. [page.tsx:1715](src/app/admin/(console)/page.tsx#L1715)

## The three things worth doing, in order

**1. Fix the orphan leak (free, biggest structural cause).** Both receipt flows upload the blob *before* the mutation that records it — [RepRegistrationTab.tsx:507](src/components/portal/RepRegistrationTab.tsx#L507), [RepAccommodationTab.tsx:2032](src/components/portal/RepAccommodationTab.tsx#L2032). If `submitOffline` then rejects (the exact-amount rule, duplicate booking, expired session, dropped network), the uploaded file is never referenced and is never deleted. Those blobs accumulate forever. Deletion only exists when the whole record is deleted ([agcAdminData.ts:2578](convex/agcAdminData.ts#L2578)). A sweep that deletes `_storage` rows with no referencing record, plus a `discardUpload` call on submit failure, both stops the growth and reclaims what is already stranded.

**2. Stop new growth at the source (already half-done).** Images are compressed client-side to WebP at 1600px/q0.82 — [imageCompress.ts:48](src/lib/imageCompress.ts#L48) — good, keep it. But PDFs pass through **untouched** by design (`SKIP_TYPES`), and a scanned PDF is easily 2–8 MB, i.e. 10–30× an equivalent photo. Either reject PDFs over ~1 MB with "photograph the receipt instead", or accept the photo-first flow only.

**3. Decide whether old receipts must be kept at all.** This is the real answer to "so I don't have to pay". Once finance confirms a payment, the durable facts are the amount, reference, date, method and reviewer — all already on the record. Keeping the image forever is a policy choice, not a requirement. A retention window (e.g. 90 days after confirmation, audited before deletion) turns storage from *growing* into *flat*, which is the only configuration where "accumulating charges" stops. If your policy does require long retention, then move the bytes: an R2 bucket with these uploaded via a Convex action and the record storing `{ bucketKey }` instead of `storageId` cuts the per-GB rate roughly in half, removes egress charges entirely, and puts the first 10 GB in the free tier. R2 is S3-compatible, so the change is contained to the upload/download helpers plus a one-off migration of existing blobs.

Two caveats on the migration: it needs your Cloudflare account and keys (I can't create those), and Convex functions can't run the S3 SDK directly without a Node action — so it's a real change, not a config toggle.

My recommendation: do (1) and (2) now, they're free and stop the bleeding; then decide (3) based on policy. Say the word and I'll implement whichever you pick.

{"kind":"tool","id":"g62iwkmQRGc","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"convex/storageMaintenance.ts","instructions":"Add the orphaned-file sweep, storage report query and client discard mutation.","content":"import { ConvexError, v } from "convex/values";
import { mutation, query } from "./_generated/server";
import type { MutationCtx, QueryCtx } from "./_generated/server";
import { requireRole, sessionTokenValidator } from "./users";
import { requireRep } from "./agcPortal";
import { writeAuditLog } from "./lib/audit";

/**
 * Orphaned file cleanup for Convex file storage.
 *
 * Every receipt, POA evidence image and Excel workbook is uploaded to storage
 * *before* the mutation that records it. When that mutation is rejected — an
 * amount mismatch, a duplicate booking, an expired session, a dropped network —
 * the uploaded blob is never referenced by any row and nothing will ever delete
 * it. Those files are what this module reclaims.
 *
 * Deleting files is unforgiving, so two rules keep it safe:
 *  1. A blob is only an orphan if NO table references it, checked across every
 *     table that can hold a storage id (see `referencedStorageIds`).
 *  2. A blob must be older than the grace window (24h by default). An upload in
 *     flight, or one sitting in an open form waiting to be submitted, is
 *     unreferenced but must not be swept out from under the user.
 */

/** Uploads younger than this are never swept — they may still be claimed. */
const DEFAULT_GRACE_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
/** Files deleted per sweep call, so one click can't blow the mutation budget. */
const MAX_BATCH = 500;

/**
 * Every storage id that some row currently owns. Keep this in step with
 * `convex/schema.ts` — a missed field here means live files get deleted.
 */
async function referencedStorageIds(
  ctx: QueryCtx | MutationCtx,
): Promise<Set<string>> {
  const referenced = new Set<string>();
  const add = (id: string | null | undefined) => {
    if (id) referenced.add(id);
  };

  // Content: hero slides, gallery albums + images, the about-page portrait and
  // tour package artwork.
  for (const row of await ctx.db.query("heroSlides").collect()) add(row.storageId);
  for (const row of await ctx.db.query("galleries").collect()) add(row.coverStorageId);
  for (const row of await ctx.db.query("galleryImages").collect()) add(row.storageId);
  for (const row of await ctx.db.query("aboutContent").collect()) {
    add(row.firstLadyImageStorageId);
  }
  for (const row of await ctx.db.query("tourPackages").collect()) {
    add(row.imageStorageId);
  }

  // AGC money records: the offline payment receipt and the POA evidence image.
  for (const row of await ctx.db.query("agcRegistrations").collect()) {
    add(row.offline?.receiptStorageId);
    add(row.poa?.evidenceStorageId);
  }
  for (const row of await ctx.db.query("agcBookings").collect()) {
    add(row.offline?.receiptStorageId);
    add(row.poa?.evidenceStorageId);
  }

  return referenced;
}

type BlobRow = { _id: string; _creationTime: number; size: number };

/** Unreferenced blobs older than the grace window, oldest first. */
async function findOrphans(ctx: QueryCtx | MutationCtx, graceMs: number) {
  const referenced = await referencedStorageIds(ctx);
  const cutoff = Date.now() - graceMs;
  const blobs = (await ctx.db.system.query("_storage").collect()) as BlobRow[];
  const orphans = blobs
    .filter((blob) => !referenced.has(blob._id) && blob._creationTime <= cutoff)
    .sort((a, b) => a._creationTime - b._creationTime);
  return { blobs, orphans };
}

/**
 * What the console shows before anyone deletes anything: how much storage is
 * live versus stranded, and the oldest offenders so an admin can sanity-check
 * that the list looks like abandoned uploads rather than real records.
 */
export const getStorageReport = query({
  args: { sessionToken: sessionTokenValidator },
  handler: async (ctx, args) => {
    await requireRole(ctx, args.sessionToken, ["admin"]);
    const { blobs, orphans } = await findOrphans(ctx, DEFAULT_GRACE_MS);

    let totalBytes = 0;
    for (const blob of blobs) totalBytes += blob.size;
    let orphanedBytes = 0;
    for (const blob of orphans) orphanedBytes += blob.size;

    return {
      totalBytes,
      fileCount: blobs.length,
      orphanedFiles: orphans.length,
      orphanedBytes,
      graceHours: DEFAULT_GRACE_MS / 3_600_000,
      oldestOrphanAt: orphans.length > 0 ? orphans[0]._creationTime : null,
      sample: orphans.slice(0, 10).map((blob) => ({
        id: blob._id,
        size: blob.size,
        createdAt: blob._creationTime,
      })),
    };
  },
});

/**
 * Delete up to `limit` orphaned blobs. Idempotent: each run re-reads the
 * reference set, so anything claimed since the last sweep is left alone.
 */
export const sweepOrphanedFiles = mutation({
  args: {
    sessionToken: sessionTokenValidator,
    limit: v.optional(v.number()),
    graceHours: v.optional(v.number()),
  },
  handler: async (ctx, args) => {
    const actor = await requireRole(ctx, args.sessionToken, ["admin"]);

    const graceHours = Math.max(1, args.graceHours ?? DEFAULT_GRACE_MS / 3_600_000);
    const limit = Math.min(
      MAX_BATCH,
      Math.max(1, Math.floor(args.limit ?? MAX_BATCH)),
    );

    const { orphans } = await findOrphans(ctx, graceHours * 3_600_000);
    const batch = orphans.slice(0, limit);

    let deleted = 0;
    let bytesFreed = 0;
    let failed = 0;
    for (const blob of batch) {
      try {
        await ctx.storage.delete(blob._id as never);
      } catch {
        // Already deleted (a concurrent sweep or a manual dashboard delete) —
        // nothing to reclaim, and it must not abort the rest of the batch.
        failed += 1;
        continue;
      }
      deleted += 1;
      bytesFreed += blob.size;
    }

    if (deleted > 0) {
      await writeAuditLog(ctx, {
        actorUserId: actor._id,
        actorEmail: actor.email,
        action: "storage.orphans_swept",
        entityType: "storage",
        summary: `Deleted ${deleted} orphaned file${deleted === 1 ? "" : "s"} (${formatMb(bytesFreed)}) from file storage`,
        metadata: { deleted, failed, bytesFreed, graceHours },
      });
    }

    return {
      deleted,
      failed,
      bytesFreed,
      remaining: Math.max(0, orphans.length - deleted),
    };
  },
});

/**
 * Delete one file the caller uploaded but could not attach to a record —
 * the client calls this when a receipt submit fails after the upload. The
 * reference check keeps a buggy or malicious caller from deleting live files.
 */
export const discardUploadedFile = mutation({
  args: {
    sessionToken: sessionTokenValidator,
    storageId: v.id("_storage"),
  },
  handler: async (ctx, args) => {
    await requireRep(ctx, args.sessionToken);

    if (referenced.has(args.storageId)) {
      return { discarded: false as const, reason: "in_use" as const };

import { useState } from "react";
import { useMutation, useQuery } from "convex/react";
import { Loader2, Trash2 } from "lucide-react";
import { toast } from "sonner";
import { api } from "@convex/_generated/api";
import { cleanErrorMessage } from "@/lib/friendlyError";
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button";
import {

  CardContent,
  CardHeader,
  CardTitle,
} from "@/components/ui/card";
import { ConfirmDeleteDialog } from "@/components/admin/ConfirmDeleteDialog";
import {
  useAdminSession,
  useSessionArgs,
} from "@/components/admin/AdminSessionProvider";

function formatBytes(bytes: number): string {
  if (bytes < 1024) return `${bytes} B`;
  if (bytes < 1024 * 1024) return `${(bytes / 1024).toFixed(1)} KB`;
  if (bytes < 1024 * 1024 * 1024) {
    return `${(bytes / (1024 * 1024)).toFixed(1)} MB`;
  }
  return `${(bytes / (1024 * 1024 * 1024)).toFixed(2)} GB`;
}

function formatDay(at: number | null): string {
  if (!at) return "—";
  return new Date(at).toLocaleDateString();
}

/**
 * Admin-only housekeeping for Convex file storage.
 *
 * Receipts, POA evidence and Excel workbooks are uploaded before the record
 * that claims them exists, so a rejected submit leaves the file behind with
 * nothing pointing at it. This panel reports how much of that has piled up and
 * clears it — with a grace window so uploads still in flight are never touched.
 */
export function StorageMaintenancePanel() {
  const { user } = useAdminSession();
  const sessionArgs = useSessionArgs();
  const isAdmin = user?.role === "admin";
  const report = useQuery(
    api.storageMaintenance.getStorageReport,
    isAdmin ? sessionArgs : "skip",
  );
  const sweep = useMutation(api.storageMaintenance.sweepOrphanedFiles);
  const [confirming, setConfirming] = useState(false);
  const [running, setRunning] = useState(false);
  const [lastRun, setLastRun] = useState<{
    deleted: number;
    bytesFreed: number;
    remaining: number;
  } | null>(null);

  if (!isAdmin) return null;

  const handleSweep = async () => {
    if (!sessionArgs) return;
    setRunning(true);
    try {
      const result = await sweep({ ...sessionArgs });
      setLastRun(result);
      if (result.deleted === 0) {
        toast.success("No orphaned files to remove");
      } else {
        toast.success(
          `Removed ${result.deleted} orphaned file${result.deleted === 1 ? "" : "s"} · ${formatBytes(result.bytesFreed)} freed`,
        );
      }
      setConfirming(false);
    } catch (err) {
      toast.error(cleanErrorMessage(err) || "Cleanup failed");
    } finally {
      setRunning(false);
    }
  };

  const orphaned = report?.orphanedFiles ?? 0;

  return (
    <>
      <Card>
        <CardHeader className="flex flex-row items-start justify-between gap-3 pb-2">
          <div>
            <CardTitle className="text-sm font-medium">File storage</CardTitle>
            <p className="mt-1 text-xs text-muted-foreground">
              Receipts, payment evidence and imported workbooks. Files that no
              record points at were left behind by a failed submission and can
              be removed.
            </p>
          </div>
          <Button
            size="sm"
            variant="outline"
            disabled={running || report === undefined || orphaned === 0}
            onClick={() => setConfirming(true)}
          >
            {running ? (
              <Loader2 className="size-4 animate-spin" />
            ) : (
              <Trash2 className="size-4" />
            )}
            {running ? "Cleaning…" : "Remove orphaned files"}
          </Button>
        </CardHeader>
        <CardContent className="space-y-3">
          {report === undefined ? (
            <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">Measuring storage…</p>
          ) : (
            <>
              <div className="grid gap-2 sm:grid-cols-3">
                <div className="rounded-lg border bg-muted/40 px-2.5 py-2">
                  <p className="text-[11px] text-muted-foreground">
                    Total in storage
                  </p>
                  <p className="text-lg font-semibold tabular-nums">
                    {formatBytes(report.totalBytes)}
                  </p>
                  <p className="text-[11px] text-muted-foreground">
                    {report.fileCount} file{report.fileCount === 1 ? "" : "s"}
                  </p>
                </div>
                <div className="rounded-lg border bg-muted/40 px-2.5 py-2">
                  <p className="text-[11px] text-muted-foreground">Orphaned</p>
                  <p className="text-lg font-semibold tabular-nums">
                    {formatBytes(report.orphanedBytes)}
                  </p>
                  <p className="text-[11px] text-muted-foreground">
                    {report.orphanedFiles} file
                    {report.orphanedFiles === 1 ? "" : "s"} unreferenced
                  </p>
                </div>
                <div className="rounded-lg border bg-muted/40 px-2.5 py-2">
                  <p className="text-[11px] text-muted-foreground">
                    Oldest orphan
                  </p>
                  <p className="text-lg font-semibold tabular-nums">
                    {formatDay(report.oldestOrphanAt)}
                  </p>
                  <p className="text-[11px] text-muted-foreground">
                    Files under {report.graceHours}h old are kept
                  </p>
                </div>
              </div>
              {report.sample.length > 0 && (
                <details className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">
                  <summary className="cursor-pointer select-none">
                    Show the {report.sample.length} oldest
                  </summary>
                  <ul className="mt-2 space-y-1 font-mono text-[11px]">
                    {report.sample.map((file) => (
                      <li key={file.id} className="flex justify-between gap-3">
                        <span className="truncate">{file.id}</span>
                        <span className="tabular-nums">
                          {formatBytes(file.size)} ·{" "}
                          {new Date(file.createdAt).toLocaleString()}
                        </span>
                      </li>
                    ))}
                  </ul>
                </details>
              )}
              {lastRun && (
                <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">
                  Last cleanup removed {lastRun.deleted} file
                  {lastRun.deleted === 1 ? "" : "s"} ({formatBytes(lastRun.bytesFreed)})
                  {lastRun.remaining > 0
                    ? ` · ${lastRun.remaining} still orphaned, run again to clear the rest`
                    : ""}
                  .
                </p>
              )}
            </>
          )}
        </CardContent>
      </Card>

      <ConfirmDeleteDialog
        open={confirming}
        onOpenChange={setConfirming}
        title={`Remove ${orphaned} orphaned file${orphaned === 1 ? "" : "s"}?`}
        description={`${formatBytes(report?.orphanedBytes ?? 0)} of uploads that no registration, booking, payment record or content row points at will be permanently deleted. Files uploaded in the last ${report?.graceHours ?? 24} hours are left alone.`}
        confirmLabel={`Remove ${orphaned}`}
        loading={running}
        onConfirm={handleSweep}
      />
    </>
  );
}

**Built it.** The sweep lives in the audit area, and every failed submit now deletes its own upload.

## Server: [storageMaintenance.ts](convex/storageMaintenance.ts)

Three functions, all in one place so the reference set is defined once:

- **`getStorageReport`** (admin only) — total bytes/files, how many blobs are unreferenced, how much space they take, the oldest orphan's date, and the 10 oldest ids so an admin can eyeball the list before agreeing.
- **`sweepOrphanedFiles`** (admin only) — deletes up to 500 unreferenced blobs per run, returns `{deleted, failed, bytesFreed, remaining}`, and writes a `storage.orphans_swept` audit entry. `remaining` lets a second click clear a large backlog.
- **`discardUploadedFile`** (rep session) — deletes one upload that no record claimed, returning `in_use` instead of deleting if a row actually references it.

Two guards matter more than the code: a blob is only an orphan if **no** table references it — checked across hero slides, galleries, gallery images, the about portrait, tour packages, and both the receipt and POA evidence fields on registrations and bookings — and nothing younger than **24 hours** is ever swept, so an upload sitting in an open form can't be pulled out from under the user.

## Client

- **`discardUpload` on failure** — all four upload-then-record paths (registration receipt, booking receipt, POA evidence in both tabs) track the uploaded id and delete the blob if the submit is rejected: amount mismatch, expired session, dropped network. Previously each retry re-uploaded and stranded the previous file, so retrying made it worse.
- **Excel workbooks** — `createBookingFromExcel` now deletes the spreadsheet after the booking is created ([agcExcel.ts](convex/agcExcel.ts)). Those were never referenced by anything: every import left a permanent copy of the workbook in storage.
- **[StorageMaintenancePanel.tsx](src/components/admin/StorageMaintenancePanel.tsx)** on the [audit page](src/app/admin/(console)/audit/page.tsx) — admin-only card showing total vs orphaned bytes, the grace window, a deletable sample list, and a confirm-gated "Remove orphaned files" button. Finance sees nothing.

## Checks

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean.
- `npx eslint` on all six touched files — clean.
- New [storageOrphans.test.ts](tests/storageOrphans.test.ts): proves a fresh upload inside the grace window is not reported, that a blob claimed by a row survives the sweep while the unclaimed one is deleted and audited, that `discardUploadedFile` refuses a live file, and that non-admins get rejected. Full suite: **34 files / 260 tests passing**.

2. **The functions aren't deployed.** The new mutation and query only exist on disk — run `npx convex dev` (and `npx convex deploy` for prod) before the panel will work. +import { writeAuditLog } from "./lib/audit";
+
+/**
+ * Orphaned file cleanup for Convex file storage.
+ *
+ * Every receipt, POA evidence image and Excel workbook is uploaded to storage
+ * *before* the mutation that records it. When that mutation is rejected — an
+ * amount mismatch, a duplicate booking, an expired session, a dropped network —
+ * the uploaded blob is never referenced by any row and nothing will ever delete
+ * it. Those files are what this module reclaims.
+ *
+ * Deleting files is unforgiving, so two rules keep it safe:
+ *  1. A blob is only an orphan if NO table references it, checked across every
+ *     table that can hold a storage id (see `referencedStorageIds`).
+ *  2. A blob must be older than the grace window (24h by default). An upload in
+ *     flight, or one sitting in an open form waiting to be submitted, is
+ *     unreferenced but must not be swept out from under the user.
+ */
+
+/** Uploads younger than this are never swept — they may still be claimed. */
+const DEFAULT_GRACE_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
+/** Files deleted per sweep call, so one click can't blow the mutation budget. */
+const MAX_BATCH = 500;
+
+/**
+ * Every storage id that some row currently owns. Keep this in step with
+ * `convex/schema.ts` — a missed field here means live files get deleted.
+ */
+async function referencedStorageIds(
+  ctx: QueryCtx | MutationCtx,
+): Promise<Set<string>> {
+  const referenced = new Set<string>();
+  const add = (id: string | null | undefined) => {
+    if (id) referenced.add(id);
+  };
+
+  // Content: hero slides, gallery albums + images, the about-page portrait and
+  // tour package artwork.
+  for (const row of await ctx.db.query("heroSlides").collect()) add(row.storageId);
+  for (const row of await ctx.db.query("galleries").collect()) add(row.coverStorageId);
+  for (const row of await ctx.db.query("galleryImages").collect()) add(row.storageId);
+  for (const row of await ctx.db.query("aboutContent").collect()) {
+    add(row.firstLadyImageStorageId);
+  }
+  for (const row of await ctx.db.query("tourPackages").collect()) {
+    add(row.imageStorageId);
+  }
+
+  // AGC money records: the offline payment receipt and the POA evidence image.
+  for (const row of await ctx.db.query("agcRegistrations").collect()) {
+    add(row.offline?.receiptStorageId);
+    add(row.poa?.evidenceStorageId);
+  }
+  for (const row of await ctx.db.query("agcBookings").collect()) {
+    add(row.offline?.receiptStorageId);
+    add(row.poa?.evidenceStorageId);
+  }
+
+  return referenced;
+}
+
+type BlobRow = { _id: string; _creationTime: number; size: number };
+
+/** Unreferenced blobs older than the grace window, oldest first. */
+async function findOrphans(ctx: QueryCtx | MutationCtx, graceMs: number) {
+  const referenced = await referencedStorageIds(ctx);
+  const cutoff = Date.now() - graceMs;
+  const blobs = (await ctx.db.system
+    .query("_storage")
+    .collect()) as unknown as BlobRow[];
+  const orphans = blobs
+    .filter((blob) => !referenced.has(blob._id) && blob._creationTime <= cutoff)
+    .sort((a, b) => a._creationTime - b._creationTime);
+  return { blobs, orphans };
+}
+
+/**
+ * What the console shows before anyone deletes anything: how much storage is
+ * live versus stranded, and the oldest offenders so an admin can sanity-check
+ * that the list looks like abandoned uploads rather than real records.
+ */
+export const getStorageReport = query({
+  args: { sessionToken: sessionTokenValidator },
+  handler: async (ctx, args) => {
+    await requireRole(ctx, args.sessionToken, ["admin"]);
+    const { blobs, orphans } = await findOrphans(ctx, DEFAULT_GRACE_MS);
+
+    let totalBytes = 0;
+    for (const blob of blobs) totalBytes += blob.size;
+    let orphanedBytes = 0;
+    for (const blob of orphans) orphanedBytes += blob.size;
+
+    return {
+      totalBytes,
+      fileCount: blobs.length,
+      orphanedFiles: orphans.length,
+      orphanedBytes,
+      graceHours: DEFAULT_GRACE_MS / 3_600_000,
+      oldestOrphanAt: orphans.length > 0 ? orphans[0]._creationTime : null,
+      sample: orphans.slice(0, 10).map((blob) => ({
+        id: blob._id,
+        size: blob.size,
+        createdAt: blob._creationTime,
+      })),
+    };
+  },
+});
+
+/**
+ * Delete up to `limit` orphaned blobs. Idempotent: each run re-reads the
+ * reference set, so anything claimed since the last sweep is left alone.
+ */
+export const sweepOrphanedFiles = mutation({
+  args: {
+    sessionToken: sessionTokenValidator,
+    limit: v.optional(v.number()),
+    graceHours: v.optional(v.number()),
+  },
+  handler: async (ctx, args) => {
+    const actor = await requireRole(ctx, args.sessionToken, ["admin"]);
+
+    const graceHours = Math.max(1, args.graceHours ?? DEFAULT_GRACE_MS / 3_600_000);
+    const limit = Math.min(
+      MAX_BATCH,
+      Math.max(1, Math.floor(args.limit ?? MAX_BATCH)),
+    );
+
+    const { orphans } = await findOrphans(ctx, graceHours * 3_600_000);
+    const batch = orphans.slice(0, limit);
+
+    let deleted = 0;
+    let bytesFreed = 0;
+    let failed = 0;
+    for (const blob of batch) {
+      try {
+        await ctx.storage.delete(blob._id as Id<"_storage">);
+      } catch {
+        // Already deleted (a concurrent sweep or a manual dashboard delete) —
+        // nothing to reclaim, and it must not abort the rest of the batch.
+        failed += 1;
+        continue;
+      }
+      deleted += 1;
+      bytesFreed += blob.size;
+    }
+
+    if (deleted > 0) {
+      await writeAuditLog(ctx, {
+        actorUserId: actor._id,
+        actorEmail: actor.email,
+        action: "storage.orphans_swept",
+        entityType: "storage",
+        summary: `Deleted ${deleted} orphaned file${deleted === 1 ? "" : "s"} (${formatMb(bytesFreed)}) from file storage`,
+        metadata: { deleted, failed, bytesFreed, graceHours },
+      });
+    }
+
+    return {
+      deleted,
+      failed,
+      bytesFreed,
+      remaining: Math.max(0, orphans.length - deleted),
+    };
+  },
+});
+
+/**
+ * Delete one file the caller uploaded but could not attach to a record —
+ * the client calls this when a receipt submit fails after the upload. The
+ * reference check keeps a buggy or malicious caller from deleting live files.
+ */
+export const discardUploadedFile = mutation({
+  args: {
+    sessionToken: sessionTokenValidator,
+    storageId: v.id("_storage"),
+  },
+  handler: async (ctx, args) => {
+    await requireRep(ctx, args.sessionToken);
+
+    const referenced = await referencedStorageIds(ctx);
+    if (referenced.has(args.storageId)) {
+      return { discarded: false as const, reason: "in_use" as const };
+    }
+
+    try {
+      await ctx.storage.delete(args.storageId);
+    } catch {
+      // Already gone — the caller's failure path is unaffected either way.
+      return { discarded: false as const, reason: "missing" as const };
+    }
+    return { discarded: true as const, reason: "orphaned" as const };
+  },
+});
+
+/** Human-readable bytes for audit summaries ("12.4 MB"). */
+function formatMb(bytes: number): string {
+  if (bytes < 1024) return `${bytes} B`;
+  if (bytes < 1024 * 1024) return `${(bytes / 1024).toFixed(1)} KB`;
+  return `${(bytes / (1024 * 1024)).toFixed(1)} MB`;
+}

+function formatBytes(bytes: number): string {
+  if (bytes < 1024) return `${bytes} B`;
+  if (bytes < 1024 * 1024) return `${(bytes / 1024).toFixed(1)} KB`;

+    return `${(bytes / (1024 * 1024)).toFixed(1)} MB`;

+function formatDay(at: number | null): string {
+  if (!at) return "—";
+  return new Date(at).toLocaleDateString();
+}
+
+/**
+ * Admin-only housekeeping for Convex file storage.
+ *
+ * Receipts, POA evidence and Excel workbooks are uploaded before the record

+    } catch (err) {

+  const orphaned = report?.orphanedFiles ?? 0;
+
+  return (
+    <>
+      <Card>

+              record points at were left behind by a failed submission and can

+          </div>

+            variant="outline"

+              <Loader2 className="size-4 animate-spin" />
+            ) : (
+              <Trash2 className="size-4" />

+            {running ? "Cleaning…" : "Remove orphaned files"}
+          </Button>
+        </CardHeader>

+            <>
+              <div className="grid gap-2 sm:grid-cols-3">
+                <div className="rounded-lg border bg-muted/40 px-2.5 py-2">
+                  <p className="text-[11px] text-muted-foreground">
+                    Total in storage
+                  </p>
+                  <p className="text-lg font-semibold tabular-nums">
+                    {formatBytes(report.totalBytes)}
+                  </p>
+                  <p className="text-[11px] text-muted-foreground">
+                    {report.fileCount} file{report.fileCount === 1 ? "" : "s"}
+                  </p>
+                </div>
+                <div className="rounded-lg border bg-muted/40 px-2.5 py-2">
+                  <p className="text-[11px] text-muted-foreground">Orphaned</p>
+                  <p className="text-lg font-semibold tabular-nums">
+                    {formatBytes(report.orphanedBytes)}
+                  </p>
+                  <p className="text-[11px] text-muted-foreground">
+                    {report.orphanedFiles} file
+                    {report.orphanedFiles === 1 ? "" : "s"} unreferenced
+                  </p>
+                </div>
+                <div className="rounded-lg border bg-muted/40 px-2.5 py-2">
+                  <p className="text-[11px] text-muted-foreground">
+                    Oldest orphan
+                  </p>
+                  <p className="text-lg font-semibold tabular-nums">
+                    {formatDay(report.oldestOrphanAt)}
+                  </p>
+                  <p className="text-[11px] text-muted-foreground">
+                    Files under {report.graceHours}h old are kept
+                  </p>
+                </div>
+              </div>
+              {report.sample.length > 0 && (
+                <details className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">
+                  <summary className="cursor-pointer select-none">
+                    Show the {report.sample.length} oldest
+                  </summary>
+                  <ul className="mt-2 space-y-1 font-mono text-[11px]">
+                    {report.sample.map((file) => (
+                      <li key={file.id} className="flex justify-between gap-3">
+                        <span className="truncate">{file.id}</span>
+                        <span className="tabular-nums">
+                          {formatBytes(file.size)} ·{" "}
+                          {new Date(file.createdAt).toLocaleString()}
+                        </span>
+                      </li>
+                    ))}
+                  </ul>
+                </details>
+              )}
+              {lastRun && (
+                <p className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">
+                  Last cleanup removed {lastRun.deleted} file
+                  {lastRun.deleted === 1 ? "" : "s"} ({formatBytes(lastRun.bytesFreed)})
+                  {lastRun.remaining > 0
+                    ? ` · ${lastRun.remaining} still orphaned, run again to clear the rest`
+                    : ""}
+                  .
+                </p>
+              )}
+            </>
+          )}
+        </CardContent>
+      </Card>
+
+      <ConfirmDeleteDialog
+        open={confirming}
+        onOpenChange={setConfirming}
+        title={`Remove ${orphaned} orphaned file${orphaned === 1 ? "" : "s"}?`}
+        description={`${formatBytes(report?.orphanedBytes ?? 0)} of uploads that no registration, booking, payment record or content row points at will be permanently deleted. Files uploaded in the last ${report?.graceHours ?? 24} hours are left alone.`}
+        confirmLabel={`Remove ${orphaned}`}
+        loading={running}
+        onConfirm={handleSweep}
+      />
+    </>
+  );
+}

+import { afterEach, expect, test, vi } from "vitest";

+ * Orphaned file cleanup: a blob no row references may be deleted, a blob a row

+async function seedAdmin(t: TestConvex) {

I signed in and walked it at 390px. The layout itself held up — but the screen around it didn't, and I found four real problems.

## What was actually wrong

**1. The stats buried the list.** Eight tiles stacked two-up ate ~460px, so the roster started around 1000px down the page: you scrolled past the tiles *and* the filters before seeing a single delegate. At 390px that's most of a phone screen on tiles alone. They're now a swipeable one-row strip below `sm` (eight-column grid from `sm` up, unchanged), with the scrollbar hidden so the cut-off third tile is the scroll affordance. Document height went from **1273px to 1007px**, and the roster is visible on the first screen.

**2. "Pending" was meaningless on a card.** The table has a `Key` header above that badge; on the phone card it sat next to "Payment first" and read like a payment state. Now reads **"Key: Pending"**.

**3. Keyboard advice on a touch screen.** "Press `/` to jump to search…" was occupying four lines right where the list begins. Hidden below `sm` — there is no slash key on a phone.

**4. The filter triggers showed raw values.** You were looking at three controls reading "all", "all", "central". The trigger now renders the label it always meant — **"Hub: Any" / "Room type: Any" / "Location: Central desk"** — and I confirmed it updates on selection ("Hub: Adenta" after picking that hub). This was pre-existing on desktop too, so it improves there as well.

Also tightened while in there: the roster no longer scrolls inside a capped box on phones (confirmed `max-height: none`, page-level scrolling only — a nested scroller is what makes a touch list feel stuck), the record sheet got safe-area padding and `overscroll-contain`, and the row checkbox got a real touch target.

## Verified working at 390px

- Tap a row → the record sheet opens fixed to the bottom (441px tall, content fits without scrolling), sheet is scrollable with `overscroll-contain`.
- Close works via both the header X and the backdrop (I checked the backdrop separately — the first attempt landed on the sheet, not the dimmer).
- The table is genuinely `display: none` on phones; the list is what renders.
- At 700px, scrolling the desk sheet sideways: checkbox/Room/Bed/Name hold at their offsets (36/72/40/268px, exactly as specified) and none of the scrolled columns bleed through.

## What I could not walk

The account signed in is check-in staff, so `/admin/accommodation` redirects to the desk — **the rooms page and its "Assign to room" sheet are still only statically checked**, not visually. That sync ([syncTours.ts](convex/lib/syncTours.ts)) did two destructive things: it **patched both seeded packages back to the hardcoded values** in [tourConfig.ts](convex/lib/tourConfig.ts) — label, dates, sites, meals, both prices, badge, order, active flag — and then **deleted every package whose slug wasn't one of those two**. So your Mountain edits were overwritten on the next visit to the page, and deleting the Monday tour guaranteed it would be re-inserted the moment you reopened the tab. Any tour you created by hand was silently deleted too. Seeding is now **insert-only**: it adds a default tour only when that slug is genuinely absent, and it never patches, never deletes. I also removed the mount-time call entirely, so nothing runs behind your back. The button is relabelled **Add missing tours** with a tooltip saying it never edits or deletes — it's the only way a deleted tour can come back now, and only when you click it. **The public page is a separate file.** [/tours](src/app/tours/page.tsx) renders from the committed manifest [toursManifest.json](src/data/toursManifest.json), not from Convex — that was deliberate so the page has no database queries and checkout still re-prices server-side. So the full edit procedure is: 1. Edit in Admin → Tours → Packages and press **Save changes**. It now persists. 2. Run `npm run tours:sync` locally — it pulls active packages from Convex and rewrites the manifest (no-op if nothing changed). 3. Commit that file and redeploy. `npm run build` runs `tours:check`, so a manifest pointing at a missing image fails the build rather than shipping broken. On the redesign: here's what I'd change and why, grounded in what the page actually does today.

## What's not working now

**The decision isn't scannable.** Two tours differ only by date, price and sites, yet each card is a tall poster: 4:3 image, title, time+meals, a 3–4 line bulleted sites list, then price at the bottom. On a phone that's roughly a full screen of scroll per tour before you can even compare $40 vs $35. The price — the thing most people look for — is the last item on every card.

**The exclusion note is the loudest thing on the page.** The Library of the Anointed banner is a red `destructive` alert sitting directly under the heading, before any tour content. Red reads as "something is broken". It's a scope clarification, not an error, and it belongs next to pricing as a footnote.

**Checkout repeats work.** The sheet's first step asks for ticket quantities again, after you already chose a tour on the page, then walks you through Tickets → Details → Review → Payment. For a two-item purchase with offline payment that's three more screens than the task needs.

**Missing the things people actually ask before paying.** Where do we depart from, and at what time? "Full day" is not enough. What's not included? What happens after I transfer the money? Payment here is bank/MoMo with manual verification, so the page should say "book → pay → we confirm your ticket" up front, not on step four.

**Dates live in prose.** `dateLabel: "Monday, November 1st"` is a string, so the page can't sort by date, show days-until, lay out a real schedule, or emit valid Event structured data for search.

## The layout I'd build

A comparison-first page, not a poster gallery.

- **Date rail under the header** — small chips reading `Mon · Nov 1 · Accra` and `Thu · Nov 4 · Mountain`, in chronological order. They double as anchors and as the thing that tells you instantly how many tours exist and when they run.
- **One horizontal row per tour on desktop**: thumbnail left, then date + label as the primary line, two or three key facts (`Full day · Breakfast snack and lunch · 3 sites`), a disclosure for the full sites list, and the price right-aligned with the select control. Everything you need to compare lines up in columns. On mobile each row collapses to a compact card — thumb, date, price, one-line facts — roughly 140px tall instead of 500.
- **"What's included / not included" behind a disclosure.** This is the single biggest height win: the sites bullets collapse by default and expand on tap.
- **Selection lives on the page, not in a sheet.** Tapping a tour adds it to a sticky summary pill/bar showing "2 tickets · $75" with one action, *Continue*. The sheet then opens on **Details** — quantity already settled, with back-to-tours as a single tap out. That turns a 4-step flow into 2.
- **A three-step "How booking works" strip** right above the total: *Pick your tours → Transfer or MoMo → Finance confirms your ticket*, with the account details reachable there. Same words as the confirmation email, so nobody is surprised at step four.

## What it needs from the data model

Two optional fields on `tourPackages` unlock most of this: `startsAt` (a real timestamp) and `departurePoint`, plus `notIncluded: string[]`. With `startsAt` the page can sort by date, render "in 3 days", and emit per-tour `Offer`/`Event` JSON-LD for search — all of which is impossible with `dateLabel` as free text. Keeping `dateLabel` as the human fallback means nothing breaks for tours you haven't dated yet.

## Order I'd do it in

1. Compact comparison rows + collapsible sites (biggest mobile win, no schema change).
2. Move the Library note to a footnote and add the booking-steps strip.
3. Collapse the checkout to Details → Review → Pay with selection already on the page.
4. Add `startsAt`/`departurePoint` and sort + structured data once you're happy with the layout.

If you want, I'll build step 1 first so you can see it on a 390px screen before committing to the rest.

One thing still outstanding from before the interrupt: `/admin/register` lets anyone create a full admin account with no first-user gate — worth closing regardless of this redesign.
