Progress note:
Pushed as `2c5dfd3`, and the status page is live in the preview panel.

## `/tours/status`

A guest who closes the confirmation screen can now come back with the reference from their email and see their booking ([TourStatusLookup](src/components/tours/TourStatusLookup.tsx)):

- **Reference + email form**, then the order: reference, name, booking date, a status badge, each ticket line with `× quantity` and line total, and the order total.
- **Status-specific guidance** — *Awaiting payment* explains to transfer or upload proof; *Payment confirmed* says bring the reference on the day; *Payment failed* asks for a clearer receipt; test bookings are labelled as holding no real tickets.
- **Receipt upload works here**, so paying hours later is no longer a dead end. It's the same [TourReceiptUploader](src/components/tours/TourReceiptUploader.tsx) now used by the checkout confirmation — extracted so the two can't drift — and it shows *View uploaded file* plus a replace button once one is on file. The query is reactive, so the receipt appears without a refresh.
- **Linked from both ends**: "Already booked? Check your order status and upload a receipt" under the tour list, and a *Check your tour order* link in the confirmation sheet.

## Access control

`tourOrders.getStatus` requires **both** the reference number and the booking email, compared case-insensitively and trimmed. Every mismatch returns `null`, so an unknown reference and a real reference probed with someone else's email are indistinguishable — the page can't be used to discover whether an order exists. It returns display fields only: no document id, no package ids, no email echo. The route is `noindex, nofollow` so per-guest data never lands in search results.

## Checks

`tsc` and eslint clean, `npm run build` passes (the route prerenders statically since the lookup only runs after submit), and **36 files / 273 tests pass** — including 3 new cases: a guest reading their own order (with `_id`/`email` explicitly asserted absent), the null-answer behaviour for wrong email, wrong reference and blank input, and the receipt URL appearing after upload.

I also drove it in the browser at 390px with a real booking: typed `HC44621` + `status-check@example.com`, got the correct order with *Awaiting Payment*, tickets and the $40 total; then a valid reference with `wrong@example.com` returned *No booking found* with no hint that the reference was real. No horizontal overflow at 390px or 1280px.

Two things to note. To do that browser check I created **one test order in your dev deployment** — reference `HC44621`, email `status-check@example.com` — which will show up in Admin → Tours → Orders; say the word and I'll add a hard-delete path to remove it, since there's currently no delete mutation for tour orders. And I couldn't exercise the actual file picker through the harness, so upload-on-status-page is covered by tests and shared code rather than a manual file drop.

import { requireRole, sessionTokenValidator } from "./users";
import { AGC_ACCOMMODATION_LABELS } from "../src/lib/agcPortal";

/**
 * Read-only delegate directory.
 *
 * One flat list of every active delegate with the rep and hub that booked them

 * point people at the right room, so it is deliberately a single query: the

 * mobile data.

 * room/assignment surface stays closed to it.
 */

const DIRECTORY_ROLES = [
  "admin",
  "accommodation",
  "accommodation_volunteer",
] as const;

function personName(firstName?: string, lastName?: string) {
  return [firstName, lastName].filter(Boolean).join(" ").trim();
}

export const listDelegateDirectory = query({
  args: { sessionToken: sessionTokenValidator },
  handler: async (ctx, args) => {
    await requireRole(ctx, args.sessionToken, [...DIRECTORY_ROLES]);

    const hubs = await ctx.db.query("agcHubs").collect();
    const hubName = new Map(hubs.map((hub) => [hub._id as string, hub.name]));

    const reps = (await ctx.db.query("agcRepresentatives").collect()).filter(
      (rep) => !rep.d [… 1,504 characters omitted]   .map((guest) => {
        const booking = bookingById.get(guest.bookingId);
        if (!booking) return null;
        const rep = repById.get(booking.repId);
        if (!rep) return null;

        const room = roomById.get(roomIdByGuest.get(guest._id) ?? "");
        return {
          guestId: guest._id,
          name:
            `${guest.title} ${guest.firstName} ${guest.lastName}`.trim() ||
            personName(guest.firstName, guest.lastName),
          gender: guest.gender as string,
          repId: rep._id as string,
          repName: personName(rep.firstName, rep.lastName) || rep.username,
          hubName: hubName.get(rep.hubId) ?? "",
          region: booking.region as string,
          bookingRef: booking.referenceNumber ?? "",
          roomName: room?.name ?? null,
          building: room?.building ?? null,
          accommodationType: room?.accommodationType ?? null,
          typeLabel: room
            ? (AGC_ACCOMMODATION_LABELS[room.accommodationType] ??
              room.accommodationType)
            : null,
          checkedIn: checkedIn.has(guest._id),
        };
      })
      .filter((row): row is NonNullable<typeof row> => row !== null);

    const repSummaries = new Map<
      string,
      {
        repId: string;
        repName: string;
        hubName: string;
        region: string;
        delegateCount: number;
        assignedCount: number;
      }
    >();
    for (const delegate of delegates) {
      const existing = repSummaries.get(delegate.repId);
      if (existing) {
        existing.delegateCount += 1;
        if (delegate.roomName) existing.assignedCount += 1;
        continue;
      }
      repSummaries.set(delegate.repId, {
        repId: delegate.repId,
        repName: delegate.repName,
        hubName: delegate.hubName,
        region: delegate.region,
        delegateCount: 1,
        assignedCount: delegate.roomName ? 1 : 0,
      });
    }

    return {
      generatedAt: Date.now(),
      reps: [...repSummaries.values()].sort(
        (a, b) =>
          a.hubName.localeCompare(b.hubName) ||
          a.repName.localeCompare(b.repName),

## The role

`accommodation_volunteer` now exists in the schema, the server role tables and the client mirror ([adminRoles.ts](src/lib/adminRoles.ts), [users.ts](convex/users.ts), [schema.ts](convex/schema.ts)). It is a venue-staff role, not an admin role: it holds no area except a new `directory` area. Because of that it inherits nothing — rooms, bookings, pools, POA, check-in and the arrival desk all reject it server-side, and [AdminShell.tsx](src/components/admin/AdminShell.tsx) redirects it to `/admin/directory` from any other console URL.

The role is fixed in the server action (`registerAccommodationVolunteer` in [authActions.ts](convex/authActions.ts)), so the form can only ever mint a read-only volunteer — the form never sends a role.
- **Admin-created**: the Team page's create form and role dropdowns already spread `VENUE_STAFF_ROLES`, so "Accommodation volunteer" appears there with no extra wiring. Covered by a test that an admin can switch an account to the role.

Short answer: **at 800 files, the impact is close to zero.** The thing that actually scales badly in this codebase is the guard that inspects storage, not the files themselves.

## Size and cost

Every upload path in this app runs through [imageCompress.ts](src/lib/imageCompress.ts) first (tour receipts, AGC registration receipts, rep accommodation receipts, gallery), which re-encodes to WebP at 1600px max edge. A phone receipt lands at roughly 150–350 KB, so 800 files is **~150–250 MB** — except PDFs, which bypass compression and can be 1–5 MB each.

Convex's file storage allowance is 1 GB included on Free/Starter ($0.033/GB-month after) and 100 GB on Professional ($0.03/GB-month), so you're using a fraction of the free inclusion ([pricing](https://www.convex.dev/pricing), [limits](https://docs.convex.dev/production/state/limits)). Data egress is 1 GB/month included on Starter at $0.132/GB after — and receipts are viewed only by admins and finance, so that's noise.

One caveat if you're on the **Free** plan specifically: it has hard caps, and 800 uncompressed PDFs at ~3 MB would be 2.4 GB, which would hit the file-storage ceiling. Images never will.

## Where files actually cost you

Each file *access* counts as a function call (1M/month included on Starter). Opening a receipt = 1 call + its bytes of egress. At your volume that's a rounding error against 1M.

The public gallery — the one thing that could generate real egress — no longer lives in storage: `<Image>` points at repo-hosted static paths, and the migration mutations delete the old blobs ([galleryStorage.ts](convex/galleryStorage.ts#L481)). So the 800 are overwhelmingly receipts and POA evidence.

## What makes the count plateau instead of grow

Your [storageMaintenance.ts](convex/storageMaintenance.ts) already does the right things:

- Confirmed payment images are deleted **15 days after confirmation** by the nightly cron, with an audit entry each.
- Deleting a tour order deletes its receipt blob too ([tourOrders.ts](convex/tourOrders.ts#L381)).
- Orphaned uploads (a submit that failed after upload) are caught by a reference-checked sweeper with a 24h grace window.

The set that never shrinks is **unconfirmed, rejected or disputed receipts and POA evidence** — deliberately, since they're payment evidence. If a pile of registrations sits in "pending verification" forever, those files sit there too.

## The real ceiling: the reference scan, not the file count

`referencedStorageIds()` does a full `.collect()` on `heroSlides`, `galleries`, `galleryImages`, `aboutContent`, `tourPackages`, `tourOrders`, `agcRegistrations`, `agcBookings` **plus every `_storage` row**, and it runs on every open of the Storage panel and every sweep batch. The nightly retention job similarly scans all registrations and bookings.

At 800 files and a few thousand rows that's milliseconds. At tens of thousands of rows it becomes heavy database I/O (that's where the "I/O" line on the bill lives), and sweeps slow down because of the full scan, not because of the blobs. Also note the sweep is **manual only** — the cron purges expired payment images but never orphans, and it's capped at 500 files per click, so if a big pile ever accumulates you'll need to click twice.

So: nothing to fix now. Open Settings → Storage once to see `totalBytes` / `orphanedFiles` for real, sweep if there are orphans, and revisit the scan only if the file count reaches the thousands or the nightly job starts running long.
